## Referência: references/squad/data/motion-tokens-guide.md

# Motion Tokens — Duration, Easing & Accessibility Guide

**Source:** Industry best practices, Razorpay Blade DS reference implementation, Val Head (Tier 2 DNA)
**Purpose:** Standard for defining motion tokens and ensuring accessibility
**v4.1:** Enriched with Val Head's 5-purpose framework and UI choreography principles

---

## Motion Token Categories

### 1. Duration

How long an animation takes.

| Token | Value | Use Case |
|-------|-------|----------|
| `duration.instant` | `0ms` | Immediate state changes (checkbox toggle) |
| `duration.fast` | `100ms` | Micro-interactions (hover, focus ring) |
| `duration.normal` | `200ms` | Standard transitions (color, opacity) |
| `duration.moderate` | `300ms` | Medium transitions (expand, slide) |
| `duration.slow` | `400ms` | Larger animations (modal enter, drawer) |
| `duration.deliberate` | `600ms` | Full-page transitions, complex orchestration |

**Rule of thumb:** The bigger the element, the longer the duration. A button hover = fast. A page transition = deliberate.

### 2. Easing

How an animation accelerates/decelerates.

| Token | Cubic Bezier | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `easing.standard` | `[0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]` | Default for most transitions |
| `easing.entrance` | `[0, 0, 0.2, 1]` | Elements entering the viewport |
| `easing.exit` | `[0.4, 0, 1, 1]` | Elements leaving the viewport |
| `easing.emphasized` | `[0.2, 0, 0, 1]` | Attention-grabbing, primary actions |
| `easing.linear` | `[0, 0, 1, 1]` | Progress bars, continuous motion |

**W3C DTCG format:**
```json
{
  "easing": {
    "standard": {
      "$value": [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1],
      "$type": "cubicBezier",
      "$description": "Default easing for standard UI transitions"
    }
  }
}
```

### 3. Motion Actions

Semantic motion patterns combining duration + easing.

| Action | Duration | Easing | Description |
|--------|----------|--------|-------------|
| `enter` | moderate | entrance | Element appears in view |
| `exit` | normal | exit | Element leaves view |
| `expand` | moderate | standard | Container grows (accordion, dropdown) |
| `collapse` | normal | standard | Container shrinks |
| `fade-in` | normal | entrance | Opacity 0 → 1 |
| `fade-out` | fast | exit | Opacity 1 → 0 |
| `slide-in` | moderate | entrance | Element slides into position |
| `slide-out` | normal | exit | Element slides out |
| `scale-up` | normal | emphasized | Element scales from small to full |
| `scale-down` | fast | exit | Element scales from full to small |

---

## CSS Custom Properties Pattern

```css
:root {
  /* Duration */
  --motion-duration-instant: 0ms;
  --motion-duration-fast: 100ms;
  --motion-duration-normal: 200ms;
  --motion-duration-moderate: 300ms;
  --motion-duration-slow: 400ms;
  --motion-duration-deliberate: 600ms;

  /* Easing */
  --motion-easing-standard: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
  --motion-easing-entrance: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1);
  --motion-easing-exit: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);
  --motion-easing-emphasized: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
}

/* Usage */
.modal-enter {
  transition: opacity var(--motion-duration-moderate) var(--motion-easing-entrance),
              transform var(--motion-duration-moderate) var(--motion-easing-entrance);
}
```

---

## prefers-reduced-motion — Mandatory Handling

### The Rule

**Never disable animation entirely. Reduce, don't remove.**

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *,
  *::before,
  *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}
```

### Better Approach — Preserve Meaning

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .modal-enter {
    /* Keep opacity (low-motion), remove transform (high-motion) */
    transition: opacity var(--motion-duration-fast) var(--motion-easing-standard);
    transform: none;
  }
}
```

### What to Reduce vs. Remove

| Keep (reduced) | Remove |
|----------------|--------|
| Opacity transitions | Bouncing/spring animations |
| Color changes | Parallax scrolling |
| Simple fades | Auto-playing animations |
| State indicators | Decorative motion |

---

## Testing Motion

### Visual Regression
- Capture before/after states (not mid-animation)
- Test both motion-enabled and reduced-motion states
- Validate duration tokens match implementation

### Accessibility Audit
- [ ] prefers-reduced-motion respected on ALL animated elements
- [ ] No animation causes seizure risk (3 flashes/second max)
- [ ] Motion is not the only way to convey information
- [ ] Autoplay content has pause/stop controls
- [ ] Animation does not block interaction

### Reference: Razorpay Blade DS
Blade DS provides a production-grade reference implementation with:
- Consistent duration/easing token scale
- Shared motion primitives across components
- prefers-reduced-motion handling on every animated component
- Storybook stories showing motion in isolation

---

## Val Head's 5-Purpose Framework (v4.1)

Every animation MUST serve at least one of these purposes. If it serves none, remove it.

| Purpose | Definition | Example |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| **Orient** | Help users understand spatial relationships | Page transitions showing view hierarchy |
| **Direct Attention** | Guide focus to important elements | Notification badge animating in |
| **Show Causality** | Demonstrate cause-and-effect | Button press triggering visible action |
| **Provide Feedback** | Confirm user actions and system state | Loading spinner, success checkmark |
| **Express Brand** | Communicate brand personality through motion | Custom easing curves, signature transitions |

### UI Choreography (Val Head)

> "Animations should feel like siblings who move similarly but are different people"

- All animations in a product should have **coherent motion character**
- Never design animations in isolation — consider the full motion vocabulary
- Start with brand **voice and tone documents** as motion character input
- Custom easing curves per brand — **never use CSS defaults** (ease, ease-in-out)

### CSS vs JavaScript Decision (Val Head)

| Use CSS | Use JavaScript |
|---------|---------------|
| Simple state transitions (hover, focus) | Chaining 3+ animations |
| Single property changes | Runtime-dynamic values |
| Performance-critical (compositor thread) | Physics-based / spring easing |
| Declarative, predictable | Complex orchestration (staggered lists) |

### Motion Audit Process (Val Head)

1. **Inventory** — Catalogue ALL existing animations (CSS + JS)
2. **Evaluate UX** — Does each animation pass the 5-purpose test?
3. **Evaluate Brand** — Does motion character match brand personality?
4. **Identify Redundancy** — Similar animations with different values?
5. **Extract Tokens** — Normalize to duration/easing token scale
6. **Create System** — Define motion token system from audit findings

> "Motion has brand personality just like color and typography" — Val Head


## Referência: references/squad/data/motion-tokens-schema.yaml

```yaml
# Motion Tokens Schema — DTCG-Compliant (W3C 2025.10)
#
# Three-layer architecture for the Kinetic Design System:
#   Layer 1: Primitive tokens (raw values)
#   Layer 2: Semantic tokens (usage intent, referencing primitives)
#   Layer 3: Component tokens (component-specific overrides, referencing semantic)
#
# Source: docs/research/2026-03-21-kinetic-design-system/03-recommendations.md
# Version: 1.0.0
# Created: 2026-03-22

schema_version: "1.0.0"
dtcg_spec: "2025.10"
description: >
  DTCG-compliant motion token schema defining duration, easing, and stagger
  scales. Three layers: primitive (raw values), semantic (usage intent), and
  component (per-component overrides). All values must pass
  prefers-reduced-motion accessibility gate.

# =============================================================================
# LAYER 1: Primitive Tokens (raw values, no semantic intent)
# =============================================================================
primitive:
  duration:
    description: "Duration scale from instant to glacial. 8 stops."
    tokens:
      instant:
        $value: "0ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Immediate state changes (checkbox toggle, radio select)"
      micro:
        $value: "50ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Imperceptible micro-feedback"
      quick:
        $value: "100ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Fast micro-interactions (hover, focus ring)"
      base:
        $value: "200ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Standard transitions (color, opacity)"
      moderate:
        $value: "300ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Medium transitions (expand, slide, modal)"
      slow:
        $value: "500ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Larger animations (drawer, page section reveal)"
      dramatic:
        $value: "800ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Hero animations, attention-grabbing entrances"
      glacial:
        $value: "1200ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Full-page transitions, complex orchestration"

  easing:
    description: "Easing curves as cubic-bezier control points."
    tokens:
      linear:
        $value: [0, 0, 1, 1]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Constant speed. Progress bars, continuous motion."
      ease-in:
        $value: [0.4, 0, 1, 1]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Accelerating. Elements exiting the viewport."
      ease-out:
        $value: [0, 0, 0.2, 1]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Decelerating. Elements entering the viewport."
      ease-in-out:
        $value: [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Standard for most UI transitions."
      spring:
        $value: [0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Overshoot for playful/spring-like feel. Approximation via cubicBezier."
        linear_alternative:
          $description: >
            Physics-based spring via CSS linear() with 45 discrete points.
            Simulates stiffness ~200, damping ~20, mass ~1 (underdamped spring
            with single overshoot). Use with @supports (animation-timing-function: linear(0, 1))
            for progressive enhancement; cubicBezier above is the fallback.
          browser_support: "Chrome 113+, Safari 17.2+, Firefox 112+ (~92% global)"
          points: 45
          $value: >-
            linear(
              0, 0.009, 0.035, 0.078, 0.136, 0.208, 0.291, 0.384, 0.484,
              0.589, 0.697, 0.805, 0.910, 1.009, 1.100, 1.181, 1.249,
              1.303, 1.342, 1.366, 1.375, 1.370, 1.352, 1.323, 1.285,
              1.240, 1.191, 1.140, 1.089, 1.041, 0.998, 0.960, 0.930,
              0.907, 0.892, 0.884, 0.883, 0.889, 0.900, 0.916, 0.935,
              0.957, 0.979, 1.000, 1.000
            )
          css_usage: |
            /* Progressive enhancement: use linear() where supported, cubicBezier fallback */
            .spring-animation {
              animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
            }
            @supports (animation-timing-function: linear(0, 1)) {
              .spring-animation {
                animation-timing-function: linear(
                  0, 0.009, 0.035, 0.078, 0.136, 0.208, 0.291, 0.384, 0.484,
                  0.589, 0.697, 0.805, 0.910, 1.009, 1.100, 1.181, 1.249,
                  1.303, 1.342, 1.366, 1.375, 1.370, 1.352, 1.323, 1.285,
                  1.240, 1.191, 1.140, 1.089, 1.041, 0.998, 0.960, 0.930,
                  0.907, 0.892, 0.884, 0.883, 0.889, 0.900, 0.916, 0.935,
                  0.957, 0.979, 1.000, 1.000
                );
              }
            }
      bounce:
        $value: [0.68, -0.55, 0.27, 1.55]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Bounce effect. Use sparingly — strong personality."
        linear_alternative:
          $description: >
            Physics-based bounce via CSS linear() with 48 discrete points.
            Simulates 3-bounce decay (primary overshoot + 2 diminishing rebounds).
            Use with @supports for progressive enhancement; cubicBezier above is fallback.
          browser_support: "Chrome 113+, Safari 17.2+, Firefox 112+ (~92% global)"
          points: 48
          $value: >-
            linear(
              0, 0.004, 0.016, 0.036, 0.064, 0.101, 0.146, 0.199, 0.260,
              0.329, 0.407, 0.492, 0.585, 0.685, 0.793, 0.907, 1.028,
              1.056, 1.076, 1.088, 1.092, 1.088, 1.076, 1.056, 1.028,
              1.000, 0.972, 0.956, 0.948, 0.948, 0.956, 0.972, 1.000,
              1.014, 1.022, 1.024, 1.022, 1.014, 1.000, 0.993, 0.989,
              0.988, 0.989, 0.993, 1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 1.000
            )
          css_usage: |
            /* Progressive enhancement: use linear() where supported, cubicBezier fallback */
            .bounce-animation {
              animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.27, 1.55);
            }
            @supports (animation-timing-function: linear(0, 1)) {
              .bounce-animation {
                animation-timing-function: linear(
                  0, 0.004, 0.016, 0.036, 0.064, 0.101, 0.146, 0.199, 0.260,
                  0.329, 0.407, 0.492, 0.585, 0.685, 0.793, 0.907, 1.028,
                  1.056, 1.076, 1.088, 1.092, 1.088, 1.076, 1.056, 1.028,
                  1.000, 0.972, 0.956, 0.948, 0.948, 0.956, 0.972, 1.000,
                  1.014, 1.022, 1.024, 1.022, 1.014, 1.000, 0.993, 0.989,
                  0.988, 0.989, 0.993, 1.000, 1.000, 1.000, 1.000
                );
              }
            }
      sharp:
        $value: [0.4, 0, 0.6, 1]
        $type: cubicBezier
        $description: "Sharp acceleration/deceleration. Emphasis."

  stagger:
    description: "Stagger delay between sequential child animations."
    tokens:
      tight:
        $value: "30ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Tight stagger for dense grids (icons, tags)"
      normal:
        $value: "60ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Standard stagger for lists and card grids"
      relaxed:
        $value: "100ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Relaxed stagger for spacious layouts"
      dramatic:
        $value: "150ms"
        $type: duration
        $description: "Dramatic stagger for hero-level reveals"

# =============================================================================
# LAYER 2: Semantic Tokens (usage intent, referencing primitive tokens)
# =============================================================================
semantic:
  description: "Semantic motion tokens organized by animation purpose."
  tokens:
    enter:
      duration: "{motion.duration.moderate}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.ease-out}"
      stagger: "{motion.stagger.normal}"
      $description: "Element appearing in view (modal, dropdown, popover)"
    exit:
      duration: "{motion.duration.base}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.ease-in}"
      stagger: "{motion.stagger.tight}"
      $description: "Element leaving view (close, dismiss)"
    feedback:
      duration: "{motion.duration.quick}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.ease-out}"
      $description: "Micro-feedback (hover, active, focus)"
    expand:
      duration: "{motion.duration.moderate}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.spring}"
      $description: "Container expansion (accordion, drawer)"
    collapse:
      duration: "{motion.duration.base}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.ease-in-out}"
      $description: "Container collapse"
    hero:
      duration: "{motion.duration.dramatic}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.spring}"
      stagger: "{motion.stagger.dramatic}"
      $description: "Hero-level entrance. Attention-grabbing."
    page:
      duration: "{motion.duration.slow}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.ease-in-out}"
      $description: "Page/route transitions"
    scroll-reveal:
      duration: "{motion.duration.moderate}"
      easing: "{motion.easing.ease-out}"
      stagger: "{motion.stagger.normal}"
      $description: "Scroll-driven reveal of sections and elements"

# =============================================================================
# LAYER 3: Component Tokens (optional overrides per component)
# =============================================================================
component:
  description: >
    Component-specific motion overrides. Each entry references semantic tokens
    and can override duration or easing for specific UI patterns.
  example:
    modal:
      enter: "{motion.semantic.enter}"
      exit: "{motion.semantic.exit}"
      overlay-fade:
        duration: "{motion.duration.base}"
        easing: "{motion.easing.ease-out}"
    tooltip:
      enter:
        duration: "{motion.duration.quick}"
        easing: "{motion.easing.ease-out}"
      exit:
        duration: "{motion.duration.quick}"
        easing: "{motion.easing.ease-in}"
    toast:
      enter:
        duration: "{motion.duration.moderate}"
        easing: "{motion.easing.spring}"
      exit:
        duration: "{motion.duration.base}"
        easing: "{motion.easing.ease-in}"

# =============================================================================
# CSS OUTPUT PATTERN
# =============================================================================
css_output:
  description: "Expected CSS custom properties output from the token system."
  default_mode: |
    :root {
      /* Primitive: Duration */
      --motion-duration-instant: 0ms;
      --motion-duration-micro: 50ms;
      --motion-duration-quick: 100ms;
      --motion-duration-base: 200ms;
      --motion-duration-moderate: 300ms;
      --motion-duration-slow: 500ms;
      --motion-duration-dramatic: 800ms;
      --motion-duration-glacial: 1200ms;

      /* Primitive: Easing */
      --motion-easing-linear: linear;
      --motion-easing-ease-in: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);
      --motion-easing-ease-out: cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1);
      --motion-easing-ease-in-out: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1);
      --motion-easing-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
      --motion-easing-bounce: cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.27, 1.55);
      --motion-easing-sharp: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.6, 1);

      /* Primitive: Stagger */
      --motion-stagger-tight: 30ms;
      --motion-stagger-normal: 60ms;
      --motion-stagger-relaxed: 100ms;
      --motion-stagger-dramatic: 150ms;

      /* Semantic */
      --motion-enter-duration: var(--motion-duration-moderate);
      --motion-enter-easing: var(--motion-easing-ease-out);
      --motion-exit-duration: var(--motion-duration-base);
      --motion-exit-easing: var(--motion-easing-ease-in);
      --motion-feedback-duration: var(--motion-duration-quick);
      --motion-feedback-easing: var(--motion-easing-ease-out);
      --motion-expand-duration: var(--motion-duration-moderate);
      --motion-expand-easing: var(--motion-easing-spring);
      --motion-hero-duration: var(--motion-duration-dramatic);
      --motion-hero-easing: var(--motion-easing-spring);
      --motion-page-duration: var(--motion-duration-slow);
      --motion-page-easing: var(--motion-easing-ease-in-out);
    }
  reduced_motion: |
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      :root {
        /* Strategy: "reduced, not removed" (D8)
           - Durations reduced to 100-300ms range, NOT zeroed
           - micro/quick/base → instant (too fast to matter)
           - moderate+ → reduced but perceptible (orientation preserved)
           - Rationale: users with vestibular disorders requested reduced motion,
             not NO motion. Zeroing causes disorientation (Val Head, WCAG). */
        --motion-duration-micro: 0ms;
        --motion-duration-quick: 0ms;
        --motion-duration-base: 0ms;
        --motion-duration-moderate: 100ms;
        --motion-duration-slow: 150ms;
        --motion-duration-dramatic: 200ms;
        --motion-duration-glacial: 300ms;

        /* Staggers: short durations kept for minimal sequential cue */
        --motion-stagger-tight: 0ms;
        --motion-stagger-normal: 0ms;
        --motion-stagger-relaxed: 20ms;
        --motion-stagger-dramatic: 30ms;

        /* Easings: replace complex curves with simple deceleration (D8)
           - spring → ease-out (remove overshoot, vestibular risk)
           - bounce → ease-out (remove oscillation, vestibular risk)
           - elastic implicit: use ease-in-out */
        --motion-easing-spring: var(--motion-easing-ease-out);
        --motion-easing-bounce: var(--motion-easing-ease-out);
      }
    }

# =============================================================================
# ACCESSIBILITY RULES
# =============================================================================
accessibility:
  rules:
    - "All motion tokens MUST respect prefers-reduced-motion"
    - "Reduced motion strategy: 'reduced, not removed' (D8) — durations 100-300ms, NOT 0ms"
    - "Easing overrides: spring → ease-out, bounce → ease-out (remove overshoot/oscillation)"
    - "Functional animations (navigation, feedback): reduce duration to 100ms with ease-out"
    - "Decorative animations (parallax, rotate, brand): remove entirely (opacity: 1, instant)"
    - "Opacity-only animations (fadeIn, fadeOut): keep — safe for vestibular disorders"
    - "Never disable animation entirely for opacity (keep instant crossfade)"
    - "Maximum flash rate: 3 per second (WCAG 2.3.1)"
    - "No animation as sole information carrier (WCAG 1.3.3)"
    - "Auto-playing content must have pause/stop controls"
  reduced_motion_strategy: "reduced-not-removed"
  reduced_motion_easing_overrides:
    spring: "ease-out"
    bounce: "ease-out"
    elastic: "ease-in-out"
  reduced_motion_duration_scale:
    micro: "0ms"
    quick: "0ms"
    base: "0ms"
    moderate: "100ms"
    slow: "150ms"
    dramatic: "200ms"
    glacial: "300ms"
  flash_limit: 3

# =============================================================================
# IMPORT STRATEGY (D1 — Motion 12)
# =============================================================================
import_strategy:
  description: >
    Motion 12 import strategy to minimize bundle size. Default import is
    motion/mini (2.3KB gzipped). Advanced features loaded via LazyMotion
    with dynamic import. NEVER import the full motion package (55-85KB).
  default_import:
    package: "motion/mini"
    size: "2.3KB gzipped"
    includes: ["animate", "initial", "exit", "variants", "transition"]
    usage: |
      import { motion } from "motion/mini"
      // Covers 90% of primitive animations (fadeIn, slideIn, scaleIn, etc.)
  advanced_import:
    package: "motion (LazyMotion)"
    size: "on-demand via dynamic import"
    includes: ["layoutId", "AnimatePresence", "useScroll", "useTransform", "drag"]
    usage: |
      import { LazyMotion, domAnimation } from "motion"
      // Wrap component tree:
      // <LazyMotion features={domAnimation}>...</LazyMotion>
      // For full features (drag, layout):
      // const loadFeatures = () => import("motion").then(mod => mod.domMax)
    when: "Compositions requiring layoutId, drag, or useScroll hooks"
  rules:
    - "NEVER import from 'motion' directly — always 'motion/mini' or LazyMotion"
    - "motion/mini is sufficient for all 10 primitives in CSS+Framer dual mode"
    - "LazyMotion required only for: layoutId (listReorder), drag, useScroll (parallax)"
    - "Bundle budget: motion layer must add < 5KB to initial bundle"

# =============================================================================
# GSAP LOADING STRATEGY (D2)
# =============================================================================
gsap_strategy:
  description: >
    GSAP is used exclusively for Layer 4+ choreographies (scroll-driven
    timelines, pin+scrub, MorphSVG). It MUST be loaded via dynamic import
    and NEVER included in the main bundle.
  loading: "dynamic import"
  size: "~23KB gzipped (core + ScrollTrigger)"
  scope: "Layer 4+ choreographies only"
  usage: |
    // Dynamic import — only when scroll choreography is needed
    const loadGSAP = async () => {
      const { gsap } = await import("gsap")
      const { ScrollTrigger } = await import("gsap/ScrollTrigger")
      gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger)
      return { gsap, ScrollTrigger }
    }
  rules:
    - "GSAP is NEVER in the main bundle — dynamic import only"
    - "Used for: scrollTimeline, heroToContent, sectionSequence choreographies"
    - "NOT used for: primitives (CSS handles those), compositions (Motion 12 handles those)"
    - "Lenis (smooth scroll) loaded alongside GSAP when scroll choreography is active"
    - "License: safe for our use case (not a competing visual builder tool)"

# =============================================================================
# FIREFOX FALLBACK STRATEGY (D6)
# =============================================================================
firefox_fallback:
  description: >
    Firefox has limited support for CSS scroll-driven animations
    (animation-timeline: scroll()). For critical scroll-triggered effects,
    use IntersectionObserver as fallback. Decorative scroll effects can
    be safely ignored (progressive enhancement).
  strategy: "IntersectionObserver for critical, ignore for decorative"
  critical_effects:
    description: "Effects that convey meaning or navigation state"
    fallback: "IntersectionObserver"
    examples:
      - "scroll-reveal (section entry): use IntersectionObserver threshold 0.15"
      - "staggerGrid on viewport entry: use IntersectionObserver with stagger via JS"
      - "heroToContent pin: use GSAP ScrollTrigger (cross-browser)"
    pattern: |
      // Fallback for scroll-driven reveal when CSS scroll() is unsupported
      const observer = new IntersectionObserver(
        (entries) => {
          entries.forEach((entry) => {
            if (entry.isIntersecting) {
              entry.target.classList.add('is-visible')
              observer.unobserve(entry.target)
            }
          })
        },
        { threshold: 0.15 }
      )
  decorative_effects:
    description: "Effects that are purely aesthetic (parallax depth, background motion)"
    fallback: "none — progressive enhancement"
    examples:
      - "parallax background layers: static position, no animation"
      - "continuous scroll-driven rotation: static, no animation"
  detection: |
    // Feature detection for CSS scroll-driven animations
    const supportsScrollTimeline = CSS.supports('animation-timeline', 'scroll()')

# =============================================================================
# LINEAR() CSS BROWSER SUPPORT (S3.1 — AC5)
# =============================================================================
linear_css_support:
  description: >
    CSS linear() easing function enables real physics-based spring and bounce
    curves via discrete point interpolation. Used as progressive enhancement
    over cubicBezier approximations in spring and bounce easing tokens.
  spec: "CSS Easing Functions Level 2"
  browser_support:
    chrome: "113+"
    safari: "17.2+"
    firefox: "112+"
    edge: "113+"
    global_coverage: "~92%"
  feature_detection: |
    @supports (animation-timing-function: linear(0, 1)) {
      /* linear() is supported — use physics-based springs */
    }
  fallback_strategy: >
    cubicBezier approximation as default, linear() via @supports progressive
    enhancement. Both produce visually similar results; linear() is more
    physically accurate (overshoot amplitude, bounce decay).
  usage_pattern: |
    /* Base: cubicBezier fallback (works everywhere) */
    --motion-easing-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);

    /* Enhancement: linear() spring (Chrome 113+, Safari 17.2+, Firefox 112+) */
    @supports (animation-timing-function: linear(0, 1)) {
      --motion-easing-spring: linear(
        0, 0.009, 0.035, 0.078, 0.136, 0.208, 0.291, 0.384, 0.484,
        0.589, 0.697, 0.805, 0.910, 1.009, 1.100, 1.181, 1.249,
        1.303, 1.342, 1.366, 1.375, 1.370, 1.352, 1.323, 1.285,
        1.240, 1.191, 1.140, 1.089, 1.041, 0.998, 0.960, 0.930,
        0.907, 0.892, 0.884, 0.883, 0.889, 0.900, 0.916, 0.935,
        0.957, 0.979, 1.000, 1.000
      );
    }

# =============================================================================
# LENIS INTEGRATION (S3.1 — AC6)
# =============================================================================
lenis_integration:
  description: >
    Lenis provides smooth scroll normalization and exposes velocity/progress
    data consumed by scroll choreographies. Loaded alongside GSAP for Layer 4+
    scroll-driven effects. Lightweight complement to ScrollTrigger.
  package: "lenis"
  version: "1.3.20"
  size: "<4KB gzipped"
  license: "MIT"
  loading: "dynamic import (alongside GSAP)"
  capabilities:
    - "Smooth scroll normalization (lerp-based)"
    - "Velocity data (px/s) for scroll-driven intensity"
    - "Progress data (0-1) for scroll position"
    - "Native GSAP ScrollTrigger integration"
    - "Touch device support with momentum"
  usage: |
    // Dynamic import — only when scroll choreography is active
    const loadLenis = async () => {
      const Lenis = (await import("lenis")).default
      const lenis = new Lenis({
        lerp: 0.1,
        duration: 1.2,
        smoothWheel: true,
        autoRaf: true
      })
      return lenis
    }
  gsap_integration: |
    // Lenis + GSAP ScrollTrigger bridge
    import Lenis from "lenis"
    import { ScrollTrigger } from "gsap/ScrollTrigger"

    const lenis = new Lenis({ lerp: 0.1, duration: 1.2, autoRaf: true })
    lenis.on("scroll", ScrollTrigger.update)
  velocity_usage: |
    // Velocity-driven intensity for scroll choreographies
    lenis.on("scroll", ({ velocity, progress, direction }) => {
      // velocity: current scroll speed in px/s
      // progress: 0-1 scroll position in document
      // direction: 1 (down) or -1 (up)

      // Example: scale parallax intensity by velocity
      const intensityFactor = Math.min(Math.abs(velocity) / 1000, 1)
    })
  rules:
    - "Lenis is NEVER in the main bundle — dynamic import only"
    - "Loaded alongside GSAP when scroll choreography is active"
    - "NOT loaded for CSS-only scroll-driven animations (scroll(), view())"
    - "Bundle budget: <4KB additional to GSAP's ~23KB"
    - "Must be destroyed on route change to prevent memory leaks: lenis.destroy()"

# =============================================================================
# DTCG TRANSITION COMPOSITE TYPE — EVALUATION (S3.1 — AC4)
# =============================================================================
dtcg_transition_evaluation:
  description: >
    Evaluation of whether semantic tokens combining duration+easing should
    use the DTCG `transition` composite type instead of separate fields.
  dtcg_transition_spec: |
    The DTCG spec (2025.10) defines a `transition` composite type:
    {
      "$type": "transition",
      "$value": {
        "duration": "300ms",
        "delay": "0ms",
        "timingFunction": [0.4, 0, 0.2, 1]
      }
    }
  current_approach: >
    Semantic tokens use separate reference fields:
      enter:
        duration: "{motion.duration.moderate}"
        easing: "{motion.easing.ease-out}"
  evaluation:
    benefits:
      - "Single token for a complete transition — simpler consumption"
      - "Fully DTCG-compliant composite type"
      - "Style Dictionary v4 resolves composites into CSS shorthand automatically"
    drawbacks:
      - "Loses flexibility to override duration/easing independently at component level"
      - "Component layer needs to override the entire composite, not just one axis"
      - "Stagger is NOT part of the transition type — would still need a separate field"
      - "Current separate-field approach already works with Style Dictionary v4"
    tooling_support:
      style_dictionary_v4: "Supports transition composite — resolves to CSS transition shorthand"
      tokens_studio: "Supports transition composite in UI"
      figma_variables: "Does NOT support transition composite natively (as of 2026-03)"
  decision: >
    DECISION: Keep current separate-field approach for semantic tokens. The
    transition composite type is valid DTCG but loses the independent
    override capability needed at the component layer (e.g., a tooltip
    overrides only duration but inherits easing from semantic). Additionally,
    stagger — critical for choreographies — has no place in the transition
    composite. The current approach is DTCG-compatible (all primitives are
    typed correctly) and more flexible for the 3-layer architecture.
    RECOMMENDATION: Revisit when Figma Variables supports transition
    composite natively, which would make the single-token approach more
    compelling for designer-developer handoff.
  confidence: "ALTA — evaluated spec, tooling, and 3-layer architecture constraints"

# =============================================================================
# VALIDATION RULES
# =============================================================================
validation:
  rules:
    - "Every primitive duration must be >= 0ms"
    - "Every easing must have exactly 4 control points (or linear_alternative with 40+ points)"
    - "Semantic tokens must reference only primitive tokens"
    - "Component tokens must reference only semantic tokens"
    - "No circular references"
    - "All tokens must have $description"
    - "Duration scale must be monotonically increasing"
    - "linear() alternatives must have >= 40 discrete points"
    - "linear() must be gated behind @supports for progressive enhancement"
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/page-layout-framework.md

---
title: "Page Layout Framework"
purpose: "Define grid systems, breakpoints, responsive techniques, and reusable layout patterns with concrete Tailwind CSS v4 classes for the Page Composer agent"
version: "1.0.0"
source: "Research: docs/research/2026-03-06-page-composition-ai-agents/"
created: "2026-03-06"
---

# Page Layout Framework

## 1. Baseline Grid System

### 1.1 Hybrid 4px Grid

All spatial values derive from a **4px base unit**. The grid operates in two modes:

| Mode   | Unit | Use Case                                      | Tailwind Multiplier |
|--------|------|-----------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| Fine   | 4px  | Icon padding, border radius, small gaps       | 1 unit = `1` (0.25rem) |
| Coarse | 8px  | Component spacing, margins, padding, gutters  | 2 units = `2` (0.5rem) |

**Rule:** Use fine (4px) for internal component adjustments. Use coarse (8px) for all layout-level spacing.

Valid spacing values (px): 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256.

### 1.2 12-Column Grid

The page grid uses 12 columns with responsive gutters:

| Breakpoint | Columns | Gutter          | Margin           | Tailwind Grid               |
|------------|---------|-----------------|------------------|------------------------------|
| default    | 4       | `gap-4` (16px)  | `px-4` (16px)    | `grid grid-cols-4 gap-4`    |
| sm (640px) | 4       | `gap-4` (16px)  | `px-6` (24px)    | `sm:grid-cols-4 sm:gap-4`   |
| md (768px) | 8       | `gap-6` (24px)  | `px-6` (24px)    | `md:grid-cols-8 md:gap-6`   |
| lg (1024px)| 12      | `gap-6` (24px)  | `px-8` (32px)    | `lg:grid-cols-12 lg:gap-6`  |
| xl (1280px)| 12      | `gap-8` (32px)  | `px-8` (32px)    | `xl:grid-cols-12 xl:gap-8`  |
| 2xl(1536px)| 12      | `gap-8` (32px)  | `px-12` (48px)   | `2xl:grid-cols-12 2xl:gap-8`|

```html
<!-- Standard 12-column page grid -->
<div class="mx-auto max-w-screen-xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
  <div class="grid grid-cols-4 gap-4 md:grid-cols-8 md:gap-6 lg:grid-cols-12 lg:gap-6 xl:gap-8">
    <!-- columns here -->
  </div>
</div>
```

---

## 2. Tailwind CSS v4 Breakpoints

| Name     | Min Width | Prefix | Target Devices            |
|----------|-----------|--------|---------------------------|
| default  | 0px       | (none) | Mobile phones (portrait)  |
| `sm`     | 640px     | `sm:`  | Mobile phones (landscape) |
| `md`     | 768px     | `md:`  | Tablets (portrait)        |
| `lg`     | 1024px    | `lg:`  | Tablets (landscape), small laptops |
| `xl`     | 1280px    | `xl:`  | Laptops, desktops         |
| `2xl`    | 1536px    | `2xl:` | Large desktops, ultra-wide|

**Approach:** Mobile-first. Write base styles for mobile, then layer up with `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`, `2xl:`.

---

## 3. Five Responsive Techniques (Fluent 2)

| # | Technique      | When to Use                        | Tailwind Implementation                                     |
|---|----------------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Reposition** | Move elements to new locations     | `flex-col lg:flex-row`, `order-1 lg:order-2`                |
| 2 | **Resize**     | Scale elements proportionally      | `w-full lg:w-1/2`, `text-base lg:text-xl`                   |
| 3 | **Reflow**     | Change grid column count           | `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3`                 |
| 4 | **Show/Hide**  | Toggle visibility per breakpoint   | `hidden lg:block`, `block md:hidden`                         |
| 5 | **Re-architect**| Completely change layout structure | `block lg:hidden` (mobile nav) + `hidden lg:flex` (desktop nav) |

### Technique Decision Matrix

| Content Type   | Mobile          | Tablet            | Desktop           |
|----------------|-----------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Navigation     | Re-architect    | Reposition        | (full nav)        |
| Hero section   | Resize          | Resize            | (full size)       |
| Card grid      | Reflow (1-col)  | Reflow (2-col)    | Reflow (3-4 col)  |
| Sidebar        | Show/Hide       | Reposition        | (sidebar visible) |
| Data table     | Re-architect    | Resize            | (full table)      |
| Footer columns | Reflow          | Reflow            | (multi-column)    |

---

## 4. Container Widths

| Tailwind Class        | Max Width | Use Case                              |
|-----------------------|-----------|---------------------------------------|
| `max-w-sm`            | 384px     | Compact cards, auth forms             |
| `max-w-md`            | 448px     | Modals, medium cards                  |
| `max-w-lg`            | 512px     | Form containers, dialogs              |
| `max-w-xl`            | 576px     | Wide forms, content cards             |
| `max-w-2xl`           | 672px     | Blog content, article body            |
| `max-w-3xl`           | 768px     | Wide content, reading pages           |
| `max-w-4xl`           | 896px     | Feature sections                      |
| `max-w-5xl`           | 1024px    | Standard page container               |
| `max-w-6xl`           | 1152px    | Wide page layouts                     |
| `max-w-7xl`           | 1280px    | Full-width sections                   |
| `max-w-screen-sm`     | 640px     | Narrow page layouts                   |
| `max-w-screen-md`     | 768px     | Tablet-optimized layouts              |
| `max-w-screen-lg`     | 1024px    | Standard desktop content              |
| `max-w-screen-xl`     | 1280px    | Default page container (recommended)  |
| `max-w-screen-2xl`    | 1536px    | Ultra-wide layouts                    |
| `max-w-prose`         | 65ch      | Optimal reading width (body text)     |
| `max-w-full`          | 100%      | Full bleed sections                   |

**Default page container:** `mx-auto max-w-screen-xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8`

---

## 5. Layout Patterns

### 5.1 Sidebar-Main

**Description:** Fixed sidebar for navigation + scrollable main content area. Primary pattern for dashboards and settings.

```
+------------------+---------------------------------------------+
|                  |                                             |
|    SIDEBAR       |              MAIN CONTENT                   |
|    (fixed)       |              (scrollable)                   |
|                  |                                             |
|  [Nav Item 1]   |  +---------------------------------------+  |
|  [Nav Item 2]   |  |  Content Area                         |  |
|  [Nav Item 3]   |  |                                       |  |
|  [Nav Item 4]   |  |                                       |  |
|                  |  +---------------------------------------+  |
|                  |                                             |
|                  |                                             |
+------------------+---------------------------------------------+

Mobile: Sidebar collapses to Sheet/Drawer (Re-architect)
```

**Tailwind Implementation:**

```html
<div class="flex h-screen">
  <!-- Sidebar: hidden on mobile, visible on lg+ -->
  <aside class="hidden lg:flex lg:w-64 lg:flex-col lg:border-r lg:border-border">
    <nav class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-4">
      <!-- NavigationMenu items -->
    </nav>
  </aside>

  <!-- Main content: scrollable -->
  <main class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto">
    <div class="mx-auto max-w-screen-xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
      <!-- Content here -->
    </div>
  </main>
</div>
```

| Property         | Value                                    |
|------------------|------------------------------------------|
| Sidebar width    | `w-64` (256px)                           |
| Sidebar border   | `border-r border-border`                 |
| Main overflow    | `overflow-y-auto`                        |
| Mobile behavior  | `hidden lg:flex` + Sheet component       |
| Column span      | Sidebar: 2-3 cols, Main: 9-10 cols       |

**Compatible page types:** Dashboard (KB2), Settings/Profile (KB2)

---

### 5.2 Hero-Content

**Description:** Full-width hero section at top followed by stacked content sections below. Standard for marketing and landing pages.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                             |
|                     HERO SECTION                            |
|                   (full width, tall)                        |
|                                                             |
|              [Headline]                                     |
|              [Subheading]                                   |
|              [CTA Button]                                   |
|                                                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                             |
|  +------------------+  +------------------+  +----------+   |
|  |    Feature 1     |  |    Feature 2     |  | Feature 3|   |
|  +------------------+  +------------------+  +----------+   |
|                                                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                             |
|                    CONTENT SECTION                           |
|                  (contained width)                           |
|                                                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       FOOTER                                |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

**Tailwind Implementation:**

```html
<div class="flex min-h-screen flex-col">
  <!-- Hero: full bleed -->
  <section class="flex min-h-[60vh] items-center justify-center bg-background px-4 py-20 sm:px-6 lg:min-h-[80vh] lg:px-8">
    <div class="mx-auto max-w-4xl text-center">
      <h1 class="text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl">
        <!-- Headline -->
      </h1>
      <p class="mt-6 text-lg text-muted-foreground sm:text-xl">
        <!-- Subheading -->
      </p>
      <div class="mt-10 flex items-center justify-center gap-4">
        <!-- CTA Buttons -->
      </div>
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- Features: contained -->
  <section class="mx-auto max-w-screen-xl px-4 py-16 sm:px-6 sm:py-20 lg:px-8 lg:py-24">
    <div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-8 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3">
      <!-- Feature Cards -->
    </div>
  </section>

  <!-- Additional sections follow same container pattern -->
</div>
```

| Property         | Value                                         |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Hero height      | `min-h-[60vh] lg:min-h-[80vh]`               |
| Hero width       | Full bleed (no max-width on section)          |
| Content container| `max-w-screen-xl` or `max-w-4xl` for text    |
| Section spacing  | `py-16 sm:py-20 lg:py-24`                    |
| Feature grid     | `grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3`  |

**Compatible page types:** Landing Page (KB2), Product/Offer (KB2)

---

### 5.3 Split-Screen

**Description:** Two equal columns side by side. Used for auth flows, comparison layouts, and visual/text pairings.

```
+-----------------------------+-----------------------------+
|                             |                             |
|         LEFT PANEL          |        RIGHT PANEL          |
|                             |                             |
|     [Image / Branding]      |     [Form / Content]        |
|                             |                             |
|                             |     [Input Field]           |
|                             |     [Input Field]           |
|                             |     [Submit Button]         |
|                             |                             |
+-----------------------------+-----------------------------+

Mobile: Stacks vertically (Reposition), left panel may hide (Show/Hide)
```

**Tailwind Implementation:**

```html
<div class="flex min-h-screen flex-col lg:flex-row">
  <!-- Left panel: hidden on mobile or shown as header -->
  <div class="hidden bg-muted lg:flex lg:w-1/2 lg:items-center lg:justify-center">
    <div class="max-w-md p-8">
      <!-- Branding / Image / Illustration -->
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- Right panel: full width on mobile, half on desktop -->
  <div class="flex w-full items-center justify-center px-4 py-12 lg:w-1/2 lg:px-8">
    <div class="mx-auto w-full max-w-sm">
      <!-- Form / Content -->
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Property         | Value                                         |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Column split     | `lg:w-1/2` each                               |
| Mobile behavior  | `flex-col lg:flex-row` (Reposition)           |
| Left panel       | `hidden lg:flex` (Show/Hide on mobile)        |
| Content max-w    | `max-w-sm` to `max-w-md` per panel           |
| Min height       | `min-h-screen`                                |

**Compatible page types:** Auth Flow (KB2)

---

### 5.4 Centered-Narrow (Manuscript)

**Description:** Single centered column optimized for reading. Content-focused layout with generous whitespace.

```
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                         HEADER/NAV                          |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                             |
|            +-------------------------------+                |
|            |                               |                |
|            |         ARTICLE TITLE         |                |
|            |                               |                |
|            |    Body text flows here in    |                |
|            |    a narrow column optimized  |                |
|            |    for reading at 65-75       |                |
|            |    characters per line.       |                |
|            |                               |                |
|            |    Images can break out to    |                |
|            |    wider width if needed.     |                |
|            |                               |                |
|            +-------------------------------+                |
|                                                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
|                          FOOTER                             |
+-------------------------------------------------------------+
```

**Tailwind Implementation:**

```html
<div class="min-h-screen">
  <!-- Header -->
  <header class="border-b border-border">
    <div class="mx-auto max-w-screen-xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8">
      <!-- Nav -->
    </div>
  </header>

  <!-- Article content: narrow centered -->
  <main class="mx-auto max-w-prose px-4 py-12 sm:px-6 sm:py-16 lg:py-20">
    <article class="prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert">
      <h1><!-- Title --></h1>
      <p><!-- Body text at optimal reading width --></p>
    </article>
  </main>

  <!-- Breakout image (wider than prose) -->
  <figure class="mx-auto max-w-4xl px-4 py-8 sm:px-6">
    <img class="w-full rounded-lg" />
  </figure>

  <!-- Back to narrow -->
  <div class="mx-auto max-w-prose px-4 sm:px-6">
    <!-- More content -->
  </div>
</div>
```

| Property         | Value                                         |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Content width    | `max-w-prose` (65ch) or `max-w-2xl` (672px)  |
| Breakout width   | `max-w-4xl` or `max-w-screen-lg`             |
| Typography       | `prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert`            |
| Vertical padding | `py-12 sm:py-16 lg:py-20`                    |
| Line length      | 65-75 characters (enforced by max-w-prose)    |

**Compatible page types:** Content/Blog (KB2)

---

### 5.5 Dashboard

**Description:** Three-region layout with sidebar navigation, top bar, and main content area containing grid of widgets.

```
+------------------+---------------------------------------------+
|                  |              TOP BAR                        |
|                  |  [Search]            [Notifications] [User] |
|                  +---------------------------------------------+
|                  |                                             |
|    SIDEBAR       |  +----------+  +----------+  +----------+  |
|                  |  |  KPI 1   |  |  KPI 2   |  |  KPI 3   |  |
|  [Dashboard]     |  +----------+  +----------+  +----------+  |
|  [Analytics]     |                                             |
|  [Users]         |  +----------------------+  +------------+  |
|  [Settings]      |  |                      |  |            |  |
|                  |  |    CHART / TABLE      |  |  ACTIVITY  |  |
|                  |  |                      |  |    FEED    |  |
|                  |  |                      |  |            |  |
|                  |  +----------------------+  +------------+  |
|                  |                                             |
+------------------+---------------------------------------------+

Mobile: Sidebar = Sheet, Top bar = simplified, KPIs stack, Grid = 1 col
```

**Tailwind Implementation:**

```html
<div class="flex h-screen overflow-hidden">
  <!-- Sidebar -->
  <aside class="hidden w-64 flex-shrink-0 border-r border-border lg:block">
    <div class="flex h-full flex-col">
      <div class="flex h-16 items-center border-b border-border px-6">
        <!-- Logo -->
      </div>
      <nav class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-4">
        <!-- NavigationMenu -->
      </nav>
    </div>
  </aside>

  <!-- Main area -->
  <div class="flex flex-1 flex-col overflow-hidden">
    <!-- Top bar -->
    <header class="flex h-16 items-center justify-between border-b border-border px-4 lg:px-6">
      <div class="flex items-center gap-4">
        <!-- Mobile menu trigger (Sheet) -->
        <!-- Search -->
      </div>
      <div class="flex items-center gap-4">
        <!-- Notifications, User menu -->
      </div>
    </header>

    <!-- Dashboard content -->
    <main class="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-4 lg:p-6">
      <!-- KPI row -->
      <div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4">
        <!-- KPI Cards -->
      </div>

      <!-- Charts + Activity -->
      <div class="mt-6 grid grid-cols-1 gap-6 lg:grid-cols-3">
        <div class="lg:col-span-2">
          <!-- Chart / Table -->
        </div>
        <div>
          <!-- Activity Feed -->
        </div>
      </div>
    </main>
  </div>
</div>
```

| Property         | Value                                         |
|------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Sidebar width    | `w-64` (256px)                                |
| Top bar height   | `h-16` (64px)                                 |
| KPI grid         | `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4` |
| Main grid        | `lg:grid-cols-3` with `lg:col-span-2`        |
| Content padding  | `p-4 lg:p-6`                                  |
| Mobile sidebar   | Sheet component triggered by hamburger        |
| Overflow         | `h-screen overflow-hidden` on root, `overflow-y-auto` on main |

**Compatible page types:** Dashboard (KB2)

## 8. Mobile-First Mandatory Patterns

> Mandatory rules for every page composition. Validated at Phase 9 (QA Gate).

### 8.1 Responsive Gaps and Paddings

Large gaps and paddings MUST scale with breakpoints. Never use fixed values above `gap-6` or `p-8`.

```html
<!-- DO -->
<div class="grid gap-4 lg:gap-8">
<div class="p-4 sm:p-8 lg:p-12">

<!-- DON'T -->
<div class="grid gap-20">
<div class="p-12 sm:p-20">
```

### 8.2 Heading Scale (3-Breakpoint Rule)

Every heading `text-3xl` or larger MUST have at least 3 breakpoints (base, sm/md, lg).

```html
<!-- DO -->
<h1 class="text-2xl sm:text-4xl lg:text-6xl">
<h2 class="text-xl sm:text-2xl lg:text-4xl">

<!-- DON'T -->
<h1 class="text-3xl sm:text-5xl">     <!-- skips from mobile to tablet -->
<h2 class="text-5xl">                  <!-- fixed, overflows on mobile -->
```

### 8.3 Button Stacking

Button groups MUST stack vertically on mobile.

```html
<!-- DO -->
<div class="flex flex-col sm:flex-row gap-3 sm:gap-4">
  <Button>Primary</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
</div>

<!-- DON'T -->
<div class="flex gap-4">
  <Button>Primary</Button>
  <Button variant="secondary">Secondary</Button>
</div>
```

### 8.4 Nav Re-architecture

If desktop navigation uses `hidden md:flex` or `hidden lg:flex`, a mobile alternative MUST exist (hamburger + drawer/sheet).

```html
<!-- DO: mobile alternative required -->
<button class="md:hidden" onClick={toggleMenu}>
  <Menu class="w-6 h-6" />
</button>
<nav class="hidden md:flex gap-4">
  <!-- Desktop nav -->
</nav>
<!-- Mobile drawer when menuOpen -->

<!-- DON'T: nav disappears on mobile -->
<nav class="hidden md:flex gap-4">
  <!-- Links inaccessible on mobile -->
</nav>
```

### 8.5 Body Text Scale

Body text MUST NOT use `text-lg` or larger as fixed size. Scale from `text-base` (mobile) to `text-lg` (desktop).

```html
<!-- DO -->
<p class="text-base sm:text-lg">

<!-- DON'T -->
<p class="text-lg">
```

### 8.6 Lazy Media Loading

Below-fold videos and images MUST use lazy loading to avoid FCP/LCP degradation on mobile devices.

```html
<!-- DO: hero (above fold) — eager load is fine -->
<video autoPlay loop muted playsInline>

<!-- DO: below fold — lazy load -->
<!-- Use IntersectionObserver to start playback -->
<!-- Or loading="lazy" for images -->
<img loading="lazy" src="..." alt="..." />
```

### 8.7 max-w Safety Check

Before using `max-w-md` (448px) or `max-w-lg` (512px), verify content fits at 375px (smallest common viewport) with side padding.

```
Viewport: 375px
- px-4 = 16px each side = 343px available
- px-6 = 24px each side = 327px available
- max-w-md (448px) > 343px = content flows to full width (safe)
- But inner content relying on max-w-md width may break
  → Always test max-w containers inside padded wrappers at 375px
```

# Page Type Patterns

## How to Use This KB

Each page type below includes:

1. **Section breakdown** -- ordered list of page sections
2. **Component map** -- shadcn/ui components used per section
3. **ASCII wireframe** -- visual structure reference
4. **Layout pattern** -- reference to the layout from [page-layout-framework.md](page-layout-framework.md) (KB1)
5. **Spacing strategy** -- reference to whitespace approach from [spacing-rhythm-system.md](spacing-rhythm-system.md) (KB4)
6. **Copy framework** -- reference to copy structure from [copy-to-layout-bridge.md](copy-to-layout-bridge.md) (KB5)

---

## 0. Design Tone Vocabulary (Buzzwords → Decisoes Concretas)

Palavras de tom visual no inicio do prompt influenciam fortemente o output (validado pela Lovable "Prompting Bible"). Use esta tabela para traduzir buzzwords em decisoes de design system:

| Buzzword | Spacing (KB4) | Typography | Colors | Layout | Componentes |
|----------|---------------|------------|--------|--------|-------------|
| **minimal** | Generous | Light weights (300-400), large scale | Monocromatico, muito branco | Centrado, narrow max-w | Poucos, sem bordas, sombras sutis |
| **premium** | Generous | Serif ou display fonts, tracking wide | Dark backgrounds, gold/accent | Full-bleed hero, large images | Cards elevados, glass morphism |
| **bold** | Balanced | Heavy weights (700-900), uppercase headings | Alto contraste, cores vibrantes | Grid assimetrico, overlaps | Badges, CTAs grandes, gradients |
| **cinematic** | Generous | Display fonts, dramatic scale (1.5+ ratio) | Dark mode, spotlight accents | Full-screen sections, parallax | Hero video/image, overlay text |
| **playful** | Balanced | Rounded fonts, varied sizes | Paleta colorida, pasteis | Grid organico, cards rotacionados | Ilustracoes, badges coloridos, tooltips |
| **developer-focused** | Compact | Monospace, code-like | Dark mode, terminal greens | Sidebar-main, data-dense | Code blocks, badges tech, tables |
| **corporate** | Balanced | Sans-serif clean, regular weights | Azul/cinza, conservador | Grid simetrico, whitespace controlado | Forms, tables, breadcrumbs |
| **editorial** | Generous | Serif body, large line-height | Preto/branco com accent unico | Centered-narrow, prose | Blockquotes, pull quotes, dropcaps |

**Uso:** Quando o usuario fornecer um buzzword no brief (Constraints → visual tone), aplicar as decisoes correspondentes nas fases 3-6 do workflow. Multiplos buzzwords podem ser combinados (ex: "premium + minimal" = generous spacing + serif fonts + monocromatico).

---

## 1. Landing Page (AIDA / StoryBrand)

**Layout pattern:** hero-content (KB1 Section 5.2)
**Spacing strategy:** Generous (KB4 Section 4.1)
**Copy framework:** AIDA or StoryBrand (KB5 Section 1)
**Eye pattern:** Z-pattern (KB5 Section 2)

### Section Breakdown

| # | Section        | AIDA Phase   | StoryBrand Phase | Purpose                              |
|---|----------------|--------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1 | Hero           | Attention    | Character+Problem| Hook visitor, state value proposition|
| 2 | Social Proof   | Attention    | Guide            | Build trust with logos/testimonials  |
| 3 | Features       | Interest     | Plan             | Show capabilities and benefits       |
| 4 | Benefits/Stats | Interest     | Success          | Quantify value                       |
| 5 | Testimonials   | Desire       | Success          | Social proof with real stories       |
| 6 | Pricing        | Desire       | Plan             | Present plans and pricing            |
| 7 | FAQ            | Desire       | --               | Handle objections                    |
| 8 | Final CTA      | Action       | CTA              | Drive conversion                     |
| 9 | Footer         | --           | --               | Navigation, legal, social links      |

### Component Map

| Section        | shadcn/ui Components                                        |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| Hero           | Button (primary CTA, secondary), Badge (new/featured)       |
| Social Proof   | Avatar, AvatarGroup (custom), Badge                         |
| Features       | Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent   |
| Benefits/Stats | Card, Badge, Progress (if animated counters)                |
| Testimonials   | Card, Avatar, Separator                                     |
| Pricing        | Card, Button, Badge (popular), Separator, Tabs (toggle)     |
| FAQ            | Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionContent|
| Final CTA      | Button (primary), Input (email capture if relevant)         |
| Footer         | Separator, NavigationMenu (or link groups)                  |

## 2. Product / Offer Page

**Layout pattern:** hero-content (KB1 Section 5.2)
**Spacing strategy:** Generous (KB4 Section 4.1)
**Copy framework:** PAS or AIDA (KB5 Section 1)
**Eye pattern:** Z-pattern (KB5 Section 2)

### Section Breakdown

| # | Section         | PAS Phase  | Purpose                               |
|---|-----------------|------------|---------------------------------------|
| 1 | Hero            | Problem    | State the problem, introduce solution |
| 2 | Benefits        | Agitation  | Deepen pain points, show benefits     |
| 3 | Demo/Screenshots| Solution   | Visual proof of the product           |
| 4 | How It Works    | Solution   | Step-by-step process explanation      |
| 5 | Pricing         | Solution   | Plans and pricing comparison          |
| 6 | FAQ             | --         | Handle objections                     |
| 7 | Final CTA       | Solution   | Drive conversion                      |
| 8 | Footer          | --         | Standard footer                       |

### Component Map

## 4. Auth Flow (Login / Signup / Reset / OTP)

**Layout pattern:** split-screen (KB1 Section 5.3) or centered-narrow (KB1 Section 5.4)
**Spacing strategy:** Balanced (KB4 Section 4.3)
**Copy framework:** Minimal -- functional microcopy
**Eye pattern:** Centered focal point

### Section Breakdown

| # | Section         | Purpose                             |
|---|-----------------|-------------------------------------|
| 1 | Brand Panel     | Logo, illustration, tagline (left)  |
| 2 | Logo            | Brand identity at top of form       |
| 3 | Form Header     | Title ("Sign In") + description     |
| 4 | Form Fields     | Email, password, etc.               |
| 5 | Social Auth     | OAuth buttons (Google, GitHub, etc.)|
| 6 | Form Footer     | Links to other auth pages           |

### Component Map

| Section         | shadcn/ui Components                                      |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|
| Brand Panel     | (custom -- not a shadcn component)                        |
| Logo            | (custom image/SVG)                                        |
| Form Header     | CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription                    |
| Form Fields     | Card, CardContent, Input, Label, Checkbox, Button         |
| Social Auth     | Button (variant="outline"), Separator ("or continue with")|
| Form Footer     | CardFooter, Button (variant="link")                       |

### Auth Page Variants

| Variant      | Fields                           | Extra Elements              |
|--------------|----------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| Login        | Email, Password                  | "Forgot password?" link     |
| Signup       | Name, Email, Password, Confirm   | Terms checkbox              |
| Reset        | Email                            | "Back to login" link        |
| OTP/Verify   | 6-digit code input               | "Resend code" link + timer  |

## 7. Page Type Selection Guide

Use this decision matrix when the Page Composer agent needs to select a template:

| Signal in Brief                            | Recommended Page Type | Layout Pattern   |
|--------------------------------------------|-----------------------|------------------|
| Marketing, conversion, value proposition   | Landing Page          | hero-content     |
| Specific product/service showcase          | Product/Offer         | hero-content     |
| Data, metrics, analytics, admin            | Dashboard             | dashboard        |
| Login, signup, password, verification      | Auth Flow             | split-screen     |
| Article, blog post, documentation          | Content/Blog          | centered-narrow  |
| User preferences, account management       | Settings/Profile      | sidebar-main     |

## Referência: references/squad/data/primitives-interface.yaml

```yaml
id: primitives-interface
version: "1.0.0"
status: active
owner: design-ops
scope: provider-consumer-contract
origin: "Wave C.1 — formalizes slides-creator boundary per ADR-018 condition #5 (architect H1)"

# Machine-readable interface contract between design-ops
# (provider of design primitives) and downstream consumers (slides-creator,
# aiox-design-starter). Eliminates "primitives vs pipelines" prose ambiguity by
# enumerating EXACTLY which primitives consumers MUST consume vs MAY re-implement.
#
# Without this file, the soft co-ownership of `deck` between design-ops and
# slides-creator drifts. With it, drift is detectable at validation time.

# =============================================================================
# CONSUMERS DECLARED
# =============================================================================
consumers:

  slides-creator:
    role: "Deck authoring pipeline owner"
    consumes_primitives:
      - id: deck_stage
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#deck_stage
        consumption: MUST
        rationale: "Deck shell with scaling, keyboard nav, slide-count, speaker notes, persistence, print-to-PDF — single source of truth"
      - id: ios_frame
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#ios_frame
        consumption: MUST_when_iOS_mockup
        rationale: "Device bezel — slides-creator MUST NOT re-roll its own iOS chrome"
      - id: android_frame
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#android_frame
        consumption: MUST_when_Android_mockup
      - id: macos_window
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#macos_window
        consumption: MUST_when_macOS_mockup
      - id: browser_window
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#browser_window
        consumption: MUST_when_browser_mockup
      - id: animations
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#animations
        consumption: MUST_when_motion
        rationale: "Stage + Sprite + Easing + interpolate — slides-creator MUST NOT import Popmotion directly without first invoking these"
      - id: design_canvas
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml#design_canvas
        consumption: MAY
        rationale: "Side-by-side variant grid — useful for slides-creator's optional variant exploration but not required"
      - id: speaker_notes_protocol
        source: data/deck-contracts-spec.yaml#speaker_notes_protocol
        consumption: MUST
        rationale: "postMessage contract is a host integration — drift breaks presenter software"
      - id: data_screen_label_attribute
        source: data/deck-contracts-spec.yaml#deck_shell#data_attributes_contract
        consumption: MUST
        rationale: "Slide identification metadata, 1-indexed, surfaces in mentioned-element blocks"

    pipelines_owned_by_slides_creator:
      - "Brief intake → deck composition workflow"
      - "Deck QA pipeline (per slides-creator squad rules)"
      - "Release/handoff to clients"
      - "Deck authoring agents (slide-chief, etc.)"

    must_not:
      - "Re-implement deck_stage scaling logic"
      - "Define a new speaker notes contract"
      - "Override the [data-screen-label] indexing convention (1-indexed mandatory)"
      - "Bypass artifact-creation primitives by hand-rolling device frames"

  aiox-design-starter:
    role: "Reference runtime for tweak protocol + provider-side primitives consumer"
    consumes_primitives:
      - id: tweak_protocol_spec
        source: data/tweak-protocol-spec.yaml
        consumption: MUST
        rationale: "Starter implements the canonical reference runtime for the protocol"
      - id: starter_components_catalog
        source: data/starter-components-catalog.yaml
        consumption: MUST_at_build_time
        rationale: "Starter provides the runtime for these primitives to consumers"
      - id: animation_primitives
        source: data/animation-primitives-contract.yaml
        consumption: MUST_when_animation
      - id: window_claude_complete
        source: data/window-claude-complete-contract.yaml
        consumption: MUST_when_AI_runtime_enabled
        rationale: "Starter provides the window.claude shim for self-contained artifacts"
      - id: artifact_file_governance
        source: squads/design-ops/data/artifact-file-governance.yaml
        consumption: SHOULD
        rationale: "File size + naming + versioning conventions"

    must_not:
      - "Mutate any file under data/ — read-only"
      - "Define a competing tweak protocol"
      - "Ship divergent versions of starter components without contract update"

# =============================================================================
# CONSUMPTION SEMANTICS
# =============================================================================
consumption_levels:
  MUST: "Consumer is required to use the primitive as-is. Re-implementing is a contract violation."
  MUST_when_X: "Consumer MUST use the primitive when condition X is met (e.g., MUST use ios_frame when producing iOS mockup)."
  MUST_at_build_time: "Consumer reads at build time, not runtime. Read-only."
  SHOULD: "Strongly recommended. Deviation requires documented rationale."
  MAY: "Optional. Consumer chooses based on context."

# =============================================================================
# CONFORMANCE VALIDATION
# =============================================================================
conformance:
  validator_planned: scripts/validate-primitives-conformance.cjs
  status: pending_implementation
  validation_rules:
    - rule: slides_creator_must_import_deck_stage
      check: "grep slides-creator/templates/* for `deck_stage.js` import; fail if any deck template lacks it"
    - rule: starter_must_implement_tweak_protocol
      check: "grep apps/aiox-design-starter/src/lib/tweak/* for protocol event handlers (__activate_edit_mode, __deactivate_edit_mode, __edit_mode_available, __edit_mode_set_keys)"
    - rule: no_duplicate_device_frame_implementations
      check: "scan slides-creator + aiox-design-starter for any local re-roll of {ios,android,macos,browser}_frame components"

# =============================================================================
# CHANGE PROPOSALS
# =============================================================================
change_proposals:
  rule: "Consumers proposing primitive extensions submit PR against data/"
  approval: "@architect + @design-chief (per CODEOWNERS pinning, ADR-018 M4)"
  example_flow:
    - step: 1
      who: slides-creator
      action: "Identifies need for new primitive (e.g., circular_progress_indicator)"
    - step: 2
      who: slides-creator
      action: "Opens PR adding entry to starter-components-catalog.yaml"
    - step: 3
      who: design-chief + architect
      action: "Reviews per CODEOWNERS"
    - step: 4
      who: aiox-design-starter
      action: "Implements runtime in parallel PR (gated on contract approval)"
    - step: 5
      who: design-chief
      action: "Merges both PRs together to maintain contract-runtime sync"

# =============================================================================
# RELATED
# =============================================================================
related:
  - squads/design-ops/data/starter-components-catalog.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/tweak-protocol-spec.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/animation-primitives-contract.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/window-claude-complete-contract.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/deck-contracts-spec.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/deliverable-kinds-registry.yaml
  - docs/adrs/ADR-018-design-ops-artifact-creation-capability.md
  - docs/adrs/ROUNDTABLE-ADR-018-2026-04-18.md
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/prompt-templates-library.md

---
title: "Prompt Templates Library"

version: "1.1.0"

created: "2026-03-08"
