```yaml
  observed in the 39 reference DS catalog. Used by `extract-from-url` and
  `ds-critical-eye-compare` to classify EXTRACTED visual style against known
  archetypes, so downstream tasks know "this is shadcn-neutral-flavored" or
  "this is carbon-enterprise-flavored" — not just "tokens extracted, good luck".

  The existing `lib/extractors.cjs detectStack()` identifies the TECHNICAL
  stack (Next.js? Tailwind? Radix?). This file complements with VISUAL
  archetype classification. They are orthogonal — a Next.js+Tailwind site
  can render Apple-glass OR Carbon-enterprise OR shadcn-neutral.

method: |
  - For each archetype, observed signature in 1-3 reference DS clones
  - Extracted 5 measurable signals from real CSS/JSON token files:
      1. radius_scale     — how rounded are corners (square/sharp/round/pill)
      2. color_saturation — oklch C value range (or hex saturation %)
      3. spacing_density  — base unit + scale length (compact vs roomy)
      4. typography_weight — heading weight + body weight balance
      5. shadow_intensity — none / subtle / medium / strong
  - Plus 2 categorical signals: theme_palette (mono / branded / colorful)
    and surface_treatment (flat / shadowed / glass / borderless)

# =============================================================================
# Archetype fingerprints
# Each archetype has measurable signal ranges for classification matching
# =============================================================================

archetypes:

  shadcn-neutral:
    description: "shadcn/ui default new-york style. Near-monochrome, slight roundness, system font. Dev tools & generic admin."
    reference_ds: ["shadcn-ui", "primer-react", "geist-ui (close)"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "moderate"        # 0.375rem-0.625rem base, 7-step
      radius_sample: "0.625rem"
      color_saturation: "near-zero"   # oklch C ≈ 0 for primary; chroma only on destructive/charts
      saturation_sample: "oklch(0.205 0 0)"
      spacing_density: "moderate"     # 4px base, 32-step
      typography_weight: "medium-bold"  # 500 medium body / 600-700 headings
      shadow_intensity: "subtle"      # 0 1-3px rgba 0.05-0.1
      theme_palette: "monochrome"
      surface_treatment: "flat-with-border"
    detection_signals:
      - "oklch() with C≈0 in :root vars"
      - "border + bg-card pattern (no shadow on cards)"
      - "data-theme attribute or .dark class"
      - "@theme inline mapping"
      - "rounded-md / rounded-lg dominates"

  carbon-enterprise:
    description: "IBM Carbon / Salesforce Lightning style. Square/sharp, IBM blue accents, dense info, weak elevation. B2B power-user."
    reference_ds: ["carbon", "lightning-design-system", "fluentui v9"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "minimal"         # 0-4px; intentionally square for data-density
      radius_sample: "0.25rem (xs only)"
      color_saturation: "moderate"    # IBM blue #0f62fe; #1677ff Ant; semantic-only saturation
      saturation_sample: "hsl(220, 100%, 53%)"
      spacing_density: "compact"      # 8px-grid; 13+ step scale
      typography_weight: "regular-semibold"  # 400 body / 600 headings (IBM Plex)
      shadow_intensity: "none-or-very-subtle"  # cards rely on borders not shadows
      theme_palette: "branded-mono"   # one strong hue (blue/orange) + grayscale
      surface_treatment: "flat-with-border"
    detection_signals:
      - "IBM Plex / Salesforce Sans font detected"
      - "border-radius ≤ 4px on buttons/cards"
      - "Inter-row borders > shadows in tables"
      - "$theme-* / $interactive-* token names (Carbon naming)"
      - "13-step or larger spacing scale"

  material-elevation:
    description: "Google Material Design 2/3. Elevation shadows, slightly rounded, color-rich. Mobile-first, Android, consumer apps."
    reference_ds: ["material-ui", "material-web"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "moderate"        # 4-12px (M2) or 8-28px (M3)
      radius_sample: "0.25rem-1rem"
      color_saturation: "high"        # tonal palettes with saturated primary
      saturation_sample: "hsl(207, 90%, 54%) — Material Blue 500"
      spacing_density: "moderate"     # 8px-grid
      typography_weight: "regular-medium"  # Roboto 400/500
      shadow_intensity: "strong"      # 5 elevation levels with progressive blur
      theme_palette: "colorful"       # tonal palette, primary/secondary/tertiary
      surface_treatment: "shadowed"
    detection_signals:
      - "Roboto font family"
      - "Multiple z-index elevation levels with shadow stacking"
      - "Material color palette names (primary-500, surface-variant)"
      - "Tonal color tokens (M3)"
      - "FAB / extended FAB patterns"

  polaris-friendly:
    description: "Shopify Polaris. Soft greens, friendly rounded, e-commerce optimistic. Conversion-focused."
    reference_ds: ["polaris-react", "polaris-tokens"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "moderate-high"   # 6-12px
      radius_sample: "0.5rem"
      color_saturation: "moderate-high"
      saturation_sample: "rgb(0, 132, 142) teal / rgb(80, 184, 60) green"
      spacing_density: "roomy"        # 4/8/12/16/20/32 — large gaps
      typography_weight: "regular-semibold"  # Inter 400/600
      shadow_intensity: "subtle"
      theme_palette: "branded-warm"
      surface_treatment: "soft-shadowed"
    detection_signals:
      - "rgb(...) values (legacy, Polaris uses RGB not oklch)"
      - "spacing-tight / spacing-loose / spacing-extra-loose names"
      - "color-{purple,indigo,teal,green,yellow,orange,red}-* token namespaces"
      - "Inter font family"

  apple-glass:
    description: "Apple HIG. Frosted glass, hairline borders, SF font, generous whitespace, restrained color. Premium consumer."
    reference_ds: ["(no public repo — extracted from apple.com domain in url-extracts)"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "high"            # 12-22px on cards, infinite on buttons
      radius_sample: "0.875rem-1.375rem"
      color_saturation: "very-low"    # near-grayscale + accent tints
      saturation_sample: "hsl(0, 0%, 96%) on light / hsl(0, 0%, 7%) on dark"
      spacing_density: "very-roomy"   # 4-8-16-24-40-64 with large jumps
      typography_weight: "regular-light-bold"  # SF Pro 400/600/700
      shadow_intensity: "subtle-with-glass"  # backdrop-filter:blur dominates
      theme_palette: "monochrome-with-accent"
      surface_treatment: "glass"      # frosted/translucent surfaces
    detection_signals:
      - "SF Pro / Helvetica Neue font family"
      - "backdrop-filter: blur in CSS"
      - "Hairline 0.5px-1px borders"
      - "ac-globalnav / ac-localnav classes (apple.com markers)"
      - "Min 24px line-heights (1.5x for body)"

  brutalist-mono:
    description: "Vercel/Geist style. High contrast, near-mono, dev-tools-aesthetic. Square or pill, no shadows."
    reference_ds: ["geist-ui", "geist-font (typeface)"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "varies"          # buttons rounded-full or square
      radius_sample: "0 OR 9999px (pill)"
      color_saturation: "none"        # pure black/white + system accents
      saturation_sample: "#000 / #fff / #888"
      spacing_density: "moderate"
      typography_weight: "regular-bold"  # Geist 400/700, no medium
      shadow_intensity: "none"        # flat by intent
      theme_palette: "monochrome"
      surface_treatment: "flat"
    detection_signals:
      - "Geist Sans / Geist Mono font"
      - "Pure black / pure white near-only colors"
      - "Border 1px subtle for separation"
      - "--geist-* CSS variables (Vercel brand markers)"

  govuk-conservative:
    description: "GOV.UK / USWDS style. High contrast for accessibility, thick borders, square corners, sans-serif. Government/civic."
    reference_ds: ["govuk-frontend", "govuk-design-system", "uswds"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "minimal"         # 0px on most components
      radius_sample: "0"
      color_saturation: "moderate"    # GOV.UK black/yellow accent only
      saturation_sample: "#1d70b8 (blue) / #ffdd00 (yellow focus ring)"
      spacing_density: "moderate"
      typography_weight: "bold-only"  # 700 dominates; legibility focus
      shadow_intensity: "none"
      theme_palette: "high-contrast"
      surface_treatment: "flat-thick-border"
    detection_signals:
      - "GDS Transport / Public Sans font family"
      - "Yellow (#ffdd00) focus indicator (mandatory)"
      - "Minimum 19px body font size (govuk-body baseline)"
      - "border-radius: 0 on most components"
      - "Skip-link patterns visible"

  porsche-precision:
    description: "Porsche/Audi/auto-luxury style. Sharp angles, restrained luxury color, technical typography. WCAG 2.2 AA strict."
    reference_ds: ["porsche-design-system", "audi-ui (archived)"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "minimal-to-moderate"  # 4-8px
      radius_sample: "0.25rem-0.5rem"
      color_saturation: "low"          # near-mono with brand accent (Porsche red)
      saturation_sample: "#d5001c (Porsche brand red, used sparingly)"
      spacing_density: "compact-roomy" # mixed; tight in nav, roomy in hero
      typography_weight: "regular-bold"  # Porsche Next 400/700
      shadow_intensity: "none"
      theme_palette: "branded-mono"
      surface_treatment: "flat-with-precise-borders"
    detection_signals:
      - "Porsche Next / Audi Type font family"
      - "WCAG 2.2 AAA compliance markers"
      - "Web Components: <p-*> or <audi-*> custom elements"
      - "Tailwind v4 + custom token namespaces"

  ant-china-enterprise:
    description: "Ant Design / TDesign style. Dense forms, blue-heavy, square corners, Chinese typography support. East Asian B2B."
    reference_ds: ["ant-design", "tdesign-react", "tdesign-vue-next"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "minimal"         # 4-6px default
      radius_sample: "0.375rem"
      color_saturation: "high"        # Ant blue #1677ff dominant
      saturation_sample: "hsl(215, 100%, 54%)"
      spacing_density: "compact"      # 14px base font, dense forms
      typography_weight: "regular"    # 400 with system fallback for CJK
      shadow_intensity: "subtle"      # cards only
      theme_palette: "branded-saturated"
      surface_treatment: "flat-with-border"
    detection_signals:
      - "Ant brand color #1677ff"
      - "14px body font (Ant default)"
      - "Noto Sans / system-ui Chinese fallbacks"
      - "ant-* class prefix in HTML"
      - "border-radius: 6px on buttons"

  marketing-gradient:
    description: "Stripe / Linear / Notion-marketing style. Gradients, generous whitespace, hero typography. Marketing/landing."
    reference_ds: ["(no canonical OS DS — extracted from stripe.com / linear.app domains)"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "high"            # 12-24px
      radius_sample: "1rem-1.5rem"
      color_saturation: "high-with-gradients"
      saturation_sample: "linear-gradient + multiple oklch hues"
      spacing_density: "very-roomy"   # large hero margins
      typography_weight: "thin-bold"  # 300/700 contrast common
      shadow_intensity: "medium"      # colored shadows tinted with brand
      theme_palette: "colorful"
      surface_treatment: "gradient"
    detection_signals:
      - "Multiple linear-gradient or radial-gradient declarations"
      - "Hero h1 ≥ 60px"
      - "Large vertical sections (py-32 / 100vh)"
      - "Custom Inter / Inter-derived font"
      - "Backdrop-filter on hero CTAs"

  community-polished:
    description: "Mantine / ChakraUI / HeroUI style. Smooth, multi-color theme system, soft shadows, generous variants. Polished open-source."
    reference_ds: ["mantine", "chakra-ui", "heroui"]
    signature:
      radius_scale: "moderate-high"   # 4-16px
      radius_sample: "0.5rem-1rem"
      color_saturation: "high"        # 14-color named palettes
      saturation_sample: "10-step gray + 13 named colors (Mantine)"
      spacing_density: "moderate"     # 5-step xs-xl
      typography_weight: "regular-bold"  # 400/600/700 (Mantine fontWeights)
      shadow_intensity: "moderate"
      theme_palette: "colorful-themable"
      surface_treatment: "soft-shadowed"
    detection_signals:
      - "MantineProvider / ChakraProvider / NextUIProvider in tree"
      - "10+ named color palettes (blue/cyan/teal/green/etc.)"
      - "primaryColor + primaryShade configuration pattern"
      - "5-step spacing (xs/sm/md/lg/xl)"

# =============================================================================
# CLASSIFICATION ALGORITHM
# How extract-from-url should match extracted tokens against archetypes
# =============================================================================

classification_algorithm:
  description: |
    Given extracted tokens (colors, radius, spacing, typography, shadows from
    `inputs/tokens-detected.json` + `inputs/css-vars-detected.json`), score
    against each archetype by counting signal matches. Highest score wins.
    Ties broken by detection_signals match count.

  scoring:
    weight_per_signal_match: 1.0
    weight_per_detection_signal: 2.0       # detection signals are strong indicators
    minimum_confidence_threshold: 3.0       # below this, classification = "unknown"
    multi_archetype_threshold: 0.8          # if top-2 within 80%, return both as candidates

  signal_extraction_from_inputs:
    radius_scale:
      source_files: ["inputs/css-vars-detected.json", "inputs/tokens-detected.json"]
      logic: "Find --radius-* or border-radius declarations, average the px/rem values"
      mapping:
        "0-2px": "minimal"
        "2-8px": "minimal-to-moderate"
        "6-14px": "moderate"
        "12-24px": "moderate-high"
        "16-32px": "high"

    color_saturation:
      source_files: ["inputs/tokens-detected.json"]
      logic: |
        For each color token, parse format. If oklch(L C H), extract C.
        If hex/hsl, convert to oklch and extract C. Average across primary slots.
      mapping:
        "C ≈ 0 (≤0.02)": "near-zero / monochrome"
        "C 0.02-0.10": "very-low / mono-with-accent"
        "C 0.10-0.18": "moderate"
        "C 0.18-0.30": "high"
        "C > 0.30 OR has gradients": "high-with-gradients"

    spacing_density:
      source_files: ["inputs/tokens-detected.json"]
      logic: "Count distinct spacing values + identify base unit"
      mapping:
        "base 4px, ≥10 steps": "moderate"
        "base 4px, 5-7 steps": "moderate"
        "base 8px, ≥10 steps": "compact"
        "base 4px, 4-6 steps with large jumps (8/16/24/40/64)": "very-roomy"

    typography_weight:
      source_files: ["inputs/font-faces.json"]
      logic: "Detect heading + body weights, classify by gap"
      mapping:
        "regular-only (400)": "regular"
        "400 body + 700 heading": "regular-bold"
        "400 body + 500 + 600 + 700": "regular-medium-semibold-bold (community-polished)"
        "300 + 700 (high contrast)": "thin-bold (marketing-gradient)"
        "700-only": "bold-only (govuk-conservative)"

    shadow_intensity:
      source_files: ["inputs/shadows.json"]
      logic: "Average alpha + spread across all shadow tokens"
      mapping:
        "no shadows or all alpha < 0.05": "none"
        "1-2 small shadows, alpha 0.05-0.10": "subtle"
        "3-4 shadows, alpha 0.10-0.20": "moderate"
        "5+ shadows or alpha > 0.20": "strong"

    surface_treatment:
      detection_logic: |
        - "glass" if backdrop-filter: blur is detected anywhere
        - "shadowed" if shadow_intensity ∈ {moderate, strong}
        - "soft-shadowed" if shadow_intensity == subtle AND radius_scale ∈ {moderate-high, high}
        - "flat-with-border" if border declarations >> shadow declarations
        - "flat-thick-border" if border-width ≥ 3px
        - "flat-with-precise-borders" if border-style: solid + low alpha + no shadows
        - "gradient" if linear-gradient OR radial-gradient detected in token-usage-graph.json

# =============================================================================
# OUTPUT CONTRACT
# What the script writes after classification
# =============================================================================

output_contract:
  file: "{output_dir}/style-fingerprint.json"
  schema:
    extracted_signals:
      radius_scale: "string (one of mapping values)"
      color_saturation: "string"
      spacing_density: "string"
      typography_weight: "string"
      shadow_intensity: "string"
      surface_treatment: "string"
    classification:
      primary_archetype: "string (archetype id) | null"
      confidence_score: "number 0-100"
      secondary_archetype: "string (id) | null (only if multi_archetype_threshold met)"
      explanation: "string (why this archetype matched, signal-by-signal)"
    archetype_distance:
      "{archetype_id}": "number (raw score before normalization)"
      # ... one entry per archetype

# =============================================================================
# Consumers
# =============================================================================

consumed_by:
  scripts:
    - squads/design-ops/scripts/extract-from-url/run.cjs       # Phase 8 (after preview render)
    - squads/design-ops/scripts/extract-from-url/lib/extractors.cjs  # New function: classifyStyle()
  tasks:
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/ds-critical-eye-compare.md       # Compare extracted style vs target archetype
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/design-compare.md                # Cross-DS comparison
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/extract-design-md-from-url.md    # Surface fingerprint in DESIGN.md prose
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/pixel-perfect-clone.md           # Use archetype to bias clone toward closest reference

# =============================================================================
# How this fits with existing detectStack()
# =============================================================================

complementarity_with_detect_stack:
  description: |
    detectStack() in lib/extractors.cjs identifies TECHNICAL stack: Next.js, Tailwind,
    Radix, GSAP, etc. — what tools/libs were used.

    Style fingerprint identifies VISUAL archetype: shadcn-neutral, apple-glass,
    carbon-enterprise, etc. — how it looks and feels.

    They are ORTHOGONAL. Examples:
      - shadcn-ui (lib) typically renders shadcn-neutral (style) — high correlation
      - Next.js (lib) can render any of the 11 archetypes — no correlation
      - GOV.UK uses Nunjucks, not React, but renders govuk-conservative — orthogonal

    Both signals together produce richer classification than either alone.
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/tier-1-token-defaults-justification.yaml

```yaml
title: "Tier-1 Token Defaults — Cross-DS Justification Matrix"
version: "1.0.0"
generated_at: "2026-04-27"
generated_by: "design-ops via meta-analysis"
purpose: |
  Justify each default value chosen in `tokens-schema-hydrated-tmpl.yaml`.
  When a business onboards or an existing app needs token review, this matrix
  shows what each reference DS does for the same token category.

  Use this to answer: "Why is sinkra-hub default {{X}} = {{Y}}?"
  Answer: trace to row below. Every default is justified by at least 3 DS.

method: |
  - Cloned 39 DS in <external-ds-checkout>/
  - Inspected concrete token files (not docs):
    - polaris-tokens/dist/{spacing,colors,typography}.json
    - mantine/.../default-theme.ts
    - chakra-ui/packages/panda-preset/src/tokens/*.ts
    - shadcn-ui/apps/v4/app/globals.css
    - primer-primitives/src/tokens/base/{size,typography}/*.json5
    - ant-design/components/theme/themes/seed.ts
    - carbon/packages/layout (Sass-based)
    - heroui/packages/styles
  - Extracted scale, naming, and unit decisions
  - Selected defaults that match ≥3 references OR have explicit rationale

# =============================================================================
# DIMENSION-BY-DIMENSION COMPARISON
# =============================================================================
dimensions:

  spacing:
    sinkra_default: "5-step named (xs/sm/md/lg/xl) + base-unit 0.25rem (4px)"
    rationale: "Mantine + HeroUI + Polaris (named); Tailwind base-unit for grid math"
    references:
      polaris:
        scale: ["none(0)", "extra-tight(4px)", "tight(8px)", "base-tight(12px)", "base(16px)", "loose(20px)", "extra-loose(32px)"]
        steps: 7
        notes: "Named scale; no numeric"
      mantine:
        scale: ["xs(10px)", "sm(12px)", "md(16px)", "lg(20px)", "xl(32px)"]
        steps: 5
        notes: "Compact 5-step; rem-based"
      chakra:
        scale: ["1..32 in 0.25rem multiples"]
        steps: 32
        notes: "Tailwind clone; numeric"
      shadcn:
        scale: ["inherits Tailwind"]
        steps: 32
        notes: "No spacing tokens — uses Tailwind defaults"
      primer:
        scale: ["base/size 2/4/6/8/12/16/24/32px"]
        steps: 9
        notes: "DTCG numeric in base/size"
    decision_log: |
      5-step named + 4px base-unit balances:
      (a) Cognitive load — named is human-readable
      (b) Tailwind compat — base 4px allows numeric multipliers when needed
      (c) shadcn compat — 4px matches Tailwind v4 convention

  font_sizes:
    sinkra_default: "8-step (xs..4xl); base=1rem (16px)"
    rationale: "Tailwind + Primer + Chakra — modern web 8-step is standard"
    references:
      tailwind:
        scale: ["xs(12)/sm(14)/base(16)/lg(18)/xl(20)/2xl(24)/3xl(30)/4xl(36)/5xl(48)/6xl(60)/7xl(72)/8xl(96)/9xl(128)"]
        steps: 13
        notes: "Maximum range; sinkra picks first 8"
      primer:
        scale: ["xs(12)/sm(14)/md(16)/lg(20)/xl(32)"]
        steps: 5
        notes: "Conservative; no 2xl-4xl"
      mantine:
        scale: ["xs(12)/sm(14)/md(16)/lg(18)/xl(20)"]
        steps: 5
        notes: "5-step; relies on heading sizes for larger"
      chakra:
        scale: ["2xs..9xl (15 steps)"]
        steps: 15
        notes: "Most granular; rare to need all"
      ant:
        scale: ["fontSize: 14px (only one)"]
        steps: 1
        notes: "Single base; sized via component classes"
    decision_log: |
      8-step from xs(12) to 4xl(36) covers 99% of UI use cases.
      Tailwind's 13-step is overkill; Mantine's 5-step lacks heading sizes.
      4xl(36) is enough for h1 in most layouts; apps can extend if needed.

  font_weights:
    sinkra_default: "4-step (regular/medium/semibold/bold)"
    rationale: "Mantine + shadcn alignment; Tailwind 9-step is overkill"
    references:
      mantine:
        scale: ["regular(400)/medium(600)/bold(700)"]
        steps: 3
        notes: "Mantine uses 600 for medium"
      tailwind:
        scale: ["thin(100)..black(900) — 9 steps"]
        steps: 9
        notes: "Most fonts only have 3-4 weights anyway"
      polaris:
        scale: ["sem tokens — usa font-stack-base only"]
        steps: 0
        notes: "Polaris doesn't expose weight tokens"
    decision_log: |
      4-step covers: body(regular), emphasis(medium), strong(semibold), heading(bold).
      Note: medium=500 (Tailwind/shadcn) NOT 600 (Mantine).
      System fonts have 400/500/600/700 reliably.

  line_height:
    sinkra_default: "3-step (tight/normal/relaxed)"
    rationale: "Pragmatic; Mantine 5-step is overkill"
    references:
      mantine:
        scale: ["xs(1.4)/sm(1.45)/md(1.55)/lg(1.6)/xl(1.65)"]
        steps: 5
      tailwind:
        scale: ["3(0.75)/4(1)/5(1.25)/6(1.5)/7(1.75)/8(2)/9(2.25)/10(2.5)"]
        steps: 8
        notes: "Numeric; less semantic"
    decision_log: |
      3-step semantic is enough:
      - tight (1.25): headings
      - normal (1.5): body — WCAG recommendation
      - relaxed (1.75): long-form reading

  radius:
    sinkra_default: "7-step (none/sm/base/md/lg/xl/2xl/full)"
    rationale: "Chakra + shadcn alignment"
    references:
      chakra:
        scale: ["none/2xs/xs/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl/full"]
        steps: 11
      mantine:
        scale: ["xs(2)/sm(4)/md(8)/lg(16)/xl(32)"]
        steps: 5
      shadcn:
        scale: ["base 0.625rem; sm/md/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl via calc()"]
        steps: 7
        notes: "Single base; multipliers via @theme inline"
    decision_log: |
      7-step is sweet spot. shadcn's calc-based scaling is elegant but harder
      to override per component. We use absolute values for clarity.

  durations:
    sinkra_default: "3-step (fast/base/slow) + instant"
    rationale: "Mantine consensus; Chakra 7-step rarely fully utilized"
    references:
      chakra:
        scale: ["fastest(50)/faster(100)/fast(150)/moderate(200)/slow(300)/slower(400)/slowest(500)"]
        steps: 7
        notes: "Most apps use 3-4 of these"
      mantine:
        scale: ["sem tokens dedicados"]
        steps: 0
      polaris:
        scale: ["sem tokens"]
        steps: 0
    decision_log: |
      3-step matches motion science:
      - 150ms (fast): perception of immediate response
      - 250ms (base): standard transition
      - 350ms (slow): page-level transitions
      <100ms feels instant; >400ms feels sluggish.

  breakpoints:
    sinkra_default: "5-step (mobile 640/tablet 768/desktop 1024/wide 1280/ultrawide 1536)"
    rationale: "Tailwind v4 + shadcn convention (sm/md/lg/xl/2xl)"
    references:
      tailwind:
        scale: ["sm(640)/md(768)/lg(1024)/xl(1280)/2xl(1536)"]
        steps: 5
      bootstrap:
        scale: ["xs(0)/sm(576)/md(768)/lg(992)/xl(1200)/xxl(1400)"]
        steps: 6
      mantine:
        scale: ["xs(36em)/sm(48em)/md(62em)/lg(75em)/xl(88em)"]
        steps: 5
        notes: "em-based"
    decision_log: |
      Tailwind v4 px-based scale wins for sinkra-hub because shadcn uses it.
      em-based (Mantine) is more accessible but requires learning curve.

  z_index:
    sinkra_default: "6-step (dropdown 1000/sticky 1100/fixed 1200/modal 1300/popover 1400/tooltip 1500)"
    rationale: "Primer ascending pattern collapsed to 6 layers"
    references:
      primer:
        scale: ["zIndex 0/100/200/300/400/500/1000"]
        steps: 7
        notes: "Most granular"
      bootstrap:
        scale: ["dropdown(1000)/sticky(1020)/fixed(1030)/modal-backdrop(1040)/modal(1050)/popover(1070)/tooltip(1080)/toast(1090)"]
        steps: 8
    decision_log: |
      6 named layers cover all ARIA + interaction patterns.
      Numeric gaps (1000/1100/1200) allow business-specific insertions.

  color_space:
    sinkra_default: "oklch"
    rationale: "shadcn 2024+ standard; perceptually uniform; CSS native"
    references:
      shadcn:
        format: "oklch(L C H)"
        notes: "Default since 2024-08; supports interpolation"
      polaris:
        format: "rgb()"
        notes: "Legacy; no perceptual uniformity"
      ant:
        format: "hex (#1677FF)"
        notes: "Hex with palette generator"
      mantine:
        format: "hex"
        notes: "10-step gray + 14 named colors"
      primer:
        format: "hsl + hex (DTCG dual)"
        notes: "Both for redundancy"
    decision_log: |
      oklch is the future:
      - CSS native (no preprocessor needed)
      - Perceptually uniform (better lightness scaling)
      - Wider gamut (P3 displays)
      - shadcn community has converged here
      Tradeoff: less browser DevTools support than hex (improving).

  theming_strategy:
    sinkra_default: "data-attribute (data-theme='dark') + .dark class"
    rationale: "shadcn pattern; SSR-safe; no React Context overhead"
    references:
      shadcn:
        method: "[data-theme=dark] or .dark"
        notes: "Works without JS framework"
      mantine:
        method: "MantineProvider colorScheme + Context"
        notes: "Requires React; Context re-renders"
      mui:
        method: "ThemeProvider + Context"
        notes: "Heavy; full theme object travels"
      ant:
        method: "ConfigProvider + algorithm (defaultAlgorithm/darkAlgorithm)"
        notes: "Most flexible but Ant-specific"
      polaris:
        method: "Compiled per-theme CSS files"
        notes: "Build-time; no runtime cost but no dynamic switch"
    decision_log: |
      data-attribute wins because:
      1. SSR-safe (no flash of light theme)
      2. Works without JS framework
      3. Easy to extend with [data-brand="aiox"] etc
      4. shadcn ecosystem already uses it
      Tradeoff: cannot do partial theming (per-component) without extra layers.

# =============================================================================
# COMPONENT TOKEN COVERAGE
# Why button/input/card and NOT 100 components?
# =============================================================================
component_coverage:
  selected: ["button", "input", "card"]
  rationale: |
    These 3 components cover ~80% of UI surface:
    - Button: every interactive action
    - Input: every form field
    - Card: every contained content area

    Other components (modal, dropdown, table, etc.) inherit from semantic
    layer; only need component tokens if visual identity diverges.

  excluded:
    modal: "Inherits surface + shadow.lg + border-radius.lg from semantic"
    dropdown: "Inherits surface + shadow.md + popover z-index"
    table: "Inherits border + foreground + spacing.md from semantic"
    toast: "Inherits semantic colors (success/warning/error)"
    avatar: "Inherits radius.full + neutrals"
    tooltip: "Inherits surface-foreground + tooltip z-index"
    tabs: "Inherits foreground + border + accent"
    accordion: "Inherits border + foreground"

# =============================================================================
# WHAT THIS MATRIX REPLACES
# =============================================================================
replaces:
  - file: "squads/design-ops/templates/tokens-schema-tmpl.yaml"
    issue: "70+ {{placeholders}} sem defaults"
    resolution: "tokens-schema-hydrated-tmpl.yaml is the new canonical template"

# =============================================================================
# CONSUMERS — tasks/workflows that should reference this matrix
# =============================================================================
consumed_by:
  tasks:
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/ds-bootstrap-starter.md      # initial token gen
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/ds-extract-tokens.md          # validate extracted vs default
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/ds-token-w3c-extract.md       # DTCG schema reference
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/f1-apply-foundations.md       # foundation step
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/ds-theme-multi-brand.md       # theming pattern reference
    - squads/design-ops/tasks/emit-design-md.md             # DESIGN.md generation
  workflows:
    - squads/design-ops/workflows/foundations-pipeline.yaml
    - squads/design-ops/workflows/dtcg-tokens-governance.yaml
    - squads/design-ops/workflows/wf-style-dictionary-token-pipeline.yaml
  rules:
    - squads/design-ops/rules/design-md-convention.md
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/token-mapping-reference.md

# Token Mapping Reference

> Mapeamento completo: Figma Token → CSS Variable → Tailwind Utility
> Gerado pela task `f1-map-tokens-to-shadcn`. Atualizado a cada execucao do pipeline.

## Status

**Completo** — Mapeamento gerado a partir dos tokens em `figma-tokens-raw.md`.

## Design Decisions

| Decisao | Valor |
|---|---|
| **Tema base** | Dark-first |
| **Primary** | Monocromatico (branco/preto — sem brand color) |
| **Destructive** | brand/Khewra (#DC625E) |
| **Success** | brand/Midori (#3A913F) |
| **Warning** | brand/Sahara (#D6A461) |
| **Info** | brand/Atmos (#77C5D5) |
| **Base radius** | radius/xxs = 6px (0.375rem) |
| **Font primary** | Outfit (headings) |
| **Font secondary** | Inter (body) |
| **Font tertiary** | JetBrains Mono (code) |

## Referência: references/squad/data/tweak-protocol-spec.yaml

```yaml
id: tweak-protocol-spec
version: "1.0.0"
status: active_contract_forward_declared
owner: design-ops
scope: provider-contract
origin: "agenmod/claw-design — Tweak Protocol (2026-04-18)"

# Live-edit protocol contract for tweakable artifacts. Contract only — the
# runtime implementation lives in Wave C per ADR-018. Consumers can start
# instrumenting artifacts against this spec now, knowing the contract is
# frozen at v1.0.0.

forward_declaration_notice:
  runtime_status: pending_wave_c
  adr: "docs/adrs/ADR-018-design-ops-artifact-creation-capability.md"
  rationale: >-
    The tweak runtime is a charter-expansion item (creator capability).
    Contract spec is provider-scope (registry/metadata) and therefore legal
    to land here in Wave B.2.2.

# =============================================================================
# PURPOSE
# =============================================================================
purpose: >-
  Enable a host page (the agent's preview pane, the review pane, or an
  embedded client portal) to provide a live-editing toolbar that mutates
  in-artifact parameters and persists those changes to disk, without
  requiring the artifact to ship with its own editor UI.

# =============================================================================
# EVENT SEQUENCE (CRITICAL — ORDER MATTERS)
# =============================================================================
event_sequence:
  ordering_rule: >-
    Register the message listener BEFORE posting __edit_mode_available.
    If the listener is registered after the announcement, the host's activate
    message can land before the handler exists and the toggle silently does
    nothing. This is the single most common failure mode of the protocol.

  step_1_register_listener:
    action: "window.addEventListener('message', handler)"
    listener_handles:
      - event_type: "__activate_edit_mode"
        handler_action: "show the Tweaks panel inside the artifact"
      - event_type: "__deactivate_edit_mode"
        handler_action: "hide the Tweaks panel"

  step_2_announce_availability:
    action: "window.parent.postMessage({type: '__edit_mode_available'}, '*')"
    fires: "once, on artifact load, AFTER step 1"
    effect: "host renders the 'Edit Mode' toggle in its toolbar"

  step_3_apply_and_persist_on_change:
    trigger: "user modifies a tweakable value in the panel"
    action_a: "apply the change live in the artifact DOM/state"
    action_b: |
      window.parent.postMessage({
        type: '__edit_mode_set_keys',
        edits: { key1: value1, key2: value2 }
      }, '*')
    semantics: "partial updates merge — only included keys are changed"
    persistence: "host parses TWEAK_DEFAULS JSON block, merges edits, writes file back"

# =============================================================================
# TWEAK_DEFAULS BLOCK
# =============================================================================
tweak_defauls_block:
  location: "inside an inline <script> tag in the root HTML file"
  cardinality: "exactly ONE block per artifact"
  marker_format: |
    const TWEAK_DEFAULS = /*EDITMODE-BEGIN*/{
      "primaryColor": "#D97757",
      "fontSize": 16,
      "dark": false
    }/*EDITMODE-END*/;
  content_rules:
    - "The block between markers MUST be valid JSON"
    - "Keys must be double-quoted strings"
    - "Values must be valid JSON primitives (string, number, boolean, array, object, null)"
    - "No JavaScript expressions — no computed keys, no comments inside the JSON"
    - "No trailing commas"
  rationale: >-
    The host writes the updated JSON back to disk on persistence. If the block
    is not parseable JSON, persistence fails silently and the user's changes
    are lost on reload.

# =============================================================================
# MESSAGE SCHEMAS
# =============================================================================
message_schemas:

  from_host_to_artifact:
    - type: "__activate_edit_mode"
      payload: {}
      direction: "window.parent -> window (host to artifact iframe)"

    - type: "__deactivate_edit_mode"
      payload: {}
      direction: "window.parent -> window"

  from_artifact_to_host:
    - type: "__edit_mode_available"
      payload: {}
      direction: "window -> window.parent"
      fires_when: "artifact has registered listeners and is ready to be toggled"

    - type: "__edit_mode_set_keys"
      payload:
        edits: "object with partial key/value updates"
      direction: "window -> window.parent"
      fires_when: "user changes a tweakable value"

# =============================================================================
# TWEAK PANEL UI GUIDELINES
# =============================================================================
panel_ui:
  positioning:
    default: "fixed overlay, typically corner or edge of viewport"
    constraint: "MUST NOT block primary artifact content when toggled off"
  content:
    per_tweakable: "label + control (slider, color picker, toggle, select)"
    grouping: "group related tweakables under collapsible sections"
  accessibility:
    - "Every control has an accessible label"
    - "Controls reachable via keyboard"
    - "Focus visible"
    - "Changes announced to screen readers via aria-live"

# =============================================================================
# FAILURE MODES & DIAGNOSTICS
# =============================================================================
failure_modes:

  - mode: "listener_not_registered_in_time"
    symptom: "Toolbar toggle appears but clicking it has no visible effect"
    cause: "__edit_mode_available posted before message listener was added"
    fix: "Register listener before posting availability (see event_sequence.ordering_rule)"

  - mode: "invalid_json_in_tweak_defauls"
    symptom: "Live edits appear to work but revert on reload"
    cause: "Host cannot parse TWEAK_DEFAULS block; silent persistence failure"
    fix: "Validate TWEAK_DEFAULS is strict JSON (no trailing commas, double-quoted keys)"

  - mode: "multiple_tweak_defauls_blocks"
    symptom: "Host writes to wrong block or fails with an error"
    cause: "Exactly one block per artifact is required"
    fix: "Consolidate into a single inline <script> block"

  - mode: "namespace_collision_with_host_page"
    symptom: "Message events trigger unexpected host actions"
    cause: "Event types are unnamespaced strings"
    fix: "Use the exact canonical types above — do not invent new __edit_mode_* types"

# =============================================================================
# BINDING TO OTHER CONTRACTS
# =============================================================================
binding:
  security:
    - spec: squads/design-ops/rules/self-contained-artifact-security.md
    - note: >-
        The message listener sees events from any origin. Always validate
        event.data.type against the allowed set; ignore unknown types.

  persistence:
    - spec: squads/design-ops/data/deck-contracts-spec.yaml#playback_persistence
    - note: >-
        Tweak state and playback state are separate concerns. Do NOT write
        tweak state into the playback localStorage key. See deck-contracts-spec
        for the canonical key pattern.

  file_governance:
    - spec: squads/design-ops/data/artifact-file-governance.yaml
    - note: "TWEAK_DEFAULS persistence is a file-rewrite operation; treat like any artifact update."

# =============================================================================
# EXAMPLE ARTIFACT INSTRUMENTATION
# =============================================================================
example:
  filename: "pricing-page-tweakable.html"
  inline_script: |
    <script>
      // 1. Define tweakable defaults (EDITMODE block required)
      const TWEAK_DEFAULS = /*EDITMODE-BEGIN*/{
        "primaryColor": "#D97757",
        "heroFontSize": 48,
        "useGradient": false
      }/*EDITMODE-END*/;

      // 2. Register message listener FIRST
      let tweakPanelOpen = false;
      window.addEventListener('message', (e) => {
        if (e.data.type === '__activate_edit_mode') {
          tweakPanelOpen = true;
          renderTweakPanel();
        } else if (e.data.type === '__deactivate_edit_mode') {
          tweakPanelOpen = false;
          hideTweakPanel();
        }
      });

      // 3. Announce availability AFTER listener is live
      window.parent.postMessage({type: '__edit_mode_available'}, '*');

      // 4. On user change in panel: apply live + persist
      function onTweakChange(key, value) {
        applyTweakLive(key, value);  // mutate DOM/state
        window.parent.postMessage({
          type: '__edit_mode_set_keys',
          edits: {[key]: value}
        }, '*');
      }
    </script>

related:
  - squads/design-ops/data/deck-contracts-spec.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/artifact-file-governance.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/data/starter-components-catalog.yaml
  - squads/design-ops/rules/self-contained-artifact-security.md
  - squads/design-ops/data/design-heuristics-from-external-prompts.yaml
  - docs/adrs/ADR-018-design-ops-artifact-creation-capability.md
```


## Referência: references/squad/data/typography-hierarchy-rules.md

---
title: "Typography Hierarchy Rules"
purpose: "Define type scale, semantic tokens, vertical rhythm, responsive typography, and heading hierarchy rules for the Page Composer agent"
version: "1.0.0"
source: "Research: docs/research/2026-03-06-page-composition-ai-agents/"
created: "2026-03-06"
---

# Typography Hierarchy Rules

## 1. Modular Scale

**Ratio:** 1.25 (Major Third)
**Base:** 16px (1rem)

The Major Third ratio produces a harmonious scale where each step is 1.25x the previous. This provides clear visual distinction between levels without excessive jumps.

### Full Type Scale

| Scale Step | Size (px) | Size (rem) | Tailwind Class  | Line Height | Tailwind LH         |
|------------|-----------|------------|-----------------|-------------|----------------------|
| 8xl        | 96px      | 6rem       | `text-8xl`      | 1.0         | `leading-none`       |
| 7xl        | 72px      | 4.5rem     | `text-7xl`      | 1.0         | `leading-none`       |
| 6xl        | 60px      | 3.75rem    | `text-6xl`      | 1.0         | `leading-none`       |
| 5xl        | 48px      | 3rem       | `text-5xl`      | 1.0         | `leading-none`       |
| 4xl        | 36px      | 2.25rem    | `text-4xl`      | 1.1         | `leading-tight`      |
| 3xl        | 30px      | 1.875rem   | `text-3xl`      | 1.2         | `leading-tight`      |
| 2xl        | 24px      | 1.5rem     | `text-2xl`      | 1.25        | `leading-snug`       |
| xl         | 20px      | 1.25rem    | `text-xl`       | 1.4         | `leading-relaxed`    |
| lg         | 18px      | 1.125rem   | `text-lg`       | 1.5         | `leading-relaxed`    |
| base       | 16px      | 1rem       | `text-base`     | 1.5         | `leading-normal`     |
| sm         | 14px      | 0.875rem   | `text-sm`       | 1.43        | `leading-normal`     |
| xs         | 12px      | 0.75rem    | `text-xs`       | 1.33        | `leading-normal`     |

### Font Weight Mapping

| Weight Name  | Value | Tailwind Class     | Use Case                          |
|--------------|-------|--------------------|------------------------------------|
| Thin         | 100   | `font-thin`        | Decorative display text only       |
| Light        | 300   | `font-light`       | Large display text                 |
| Normal       | 400   | `font-normal`      | Body text, descriptions            |
| Medium       | 500   | `font-medium`      | Labels, navigation, emphasis       |
| Semibold     | 600   | `font-semibold`    | Headings, subheadings              |
| Bold         | 700   | `font-bold`        | Primary headings, strong emphasis  |
| Extrabold    | 800   | `font-extrabold`   | Hero headlines, display text       |

---

## 2. Semantic Token System

These semantic tokens map design intent to Tailwind classes. Use the semantic name when reasoning about typography; apply the Tailwind classes in code.

### Display Tokens (Hero and Marketing)

| Token        | Tailwind Classes                                                    | Use Case                   |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| display-2xl  | `text-5xl font-extrabold tracking-tight sm:text-6xl lg:text-7xl`   | Hero headline (landing)    |
| display-xl   | `text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl`        | Hero headline (product)    |
| display-lg   | `text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight sm:text-4xl lg:text-5xl`        | Section hero               |

### Heading Tokens (Structural)

| Token        | Tailwind Classes                                                    | Use Case                   |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| heading-xl   | `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-3xl lg:text-4xl`    | Section title (H2)         |
| heading-lg   | `text-xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-2xl lg:text-3xl`     | Subsection title (H3)      |
| heading-md   | `text-lg font-semibold sm:text-xl`                                  | Card title, group head (H4)|
| heading-sm   | `text-base font-semibold`                                           | Small heading (H5)         |
| heading-xs   | `text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide`                     | Overline, label heading    |

### Body Tokens (Content)

| Token        | Tailwind Classes                                                    | Use Case                   |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| body-lg      | `text-lg leading-relaxed text-foreground`                           | Lead paragraph, intro      |
| body-md      | `text-base leading-relaxed text-foreground`                         | Standard body text         |
| body-sm      | `text-sm leading-normal text-muted-foreground`                      | Secondary text, metadata   |

### Caption/Utility Tokens

| Token        | Tailwind Classes                                                    | Use Case                   |
|--------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| caption      | `text-xs leading-normal text-muted-foreground`                      | Footnotes, timestamps      |
| overline     | `text-xs font-medium uppercase tracking-widest text-muted-foreground` | Category labels, badges |
| code         | `font-mono text-sm`                                                 | Inline code, technical     |
| code-block   | `font-mono text-sm leading-relaxed`                                 | Code blocks                |

---

## 3. Vertical Rhythm

### Baseline

**Baseline unit:** 24px (1.5rem) -- derived from `text-base` (16px) with `leading-normal` (1.5).

All vertical margins and paddings should be multiples of the 24px baseline to maintain consistent rhythm.

| Multiplier | Value (px) | Value (rem) | Tailwind Class | Use Case                    |
|------------|-----------|-------------|----------------|-----------------------------|
| 0.5x       | 12px      | 0.75rem     | `mt-3`         | Within tight groups          |
| 1x         | 24px      | 1.5rem      | `mt-6`         | Between paragraphs           |
| 1.5x       | 36px      | 2.25rem     | `mt-9`         | Between subsections          |
| 2x         | 48px      | 3rem        | `mt-12`        | Between sections             |
| 3x         | 72px      | 4.5rem      | `mt-18`        | Major section breaks         |
| 4x         | 96px      | 6rem        | `mt-24`        | Page-level section gaps      |

### Heading Margin Rules

| Element | Margin Top       | Margin Bottom    | Rule                                     |
|---------|------------------|------------------|------------------------------------------|
| H1      | `mt-0`           | `mb-6`           | First element; space below for subtitle  |
| H2      | `mt-12`          | `mb-6`           | Major section break above                |
| H3      | `mt-9`           | `mb-4`           | Subsection break above                   |
| H4      | `mt-6`           | `mb-3`           | Group heading                            |
| H5      | `mt-6`           | `mb-2`           | Minor heading                            |
| p       | `mt-0`           | `mb-4`  or `mb-6`| Paragraph spacing, tighter in cards      |
| ul/ol   | `mt-4`           | `mb-4`           | List spacing                             |

---

## 4. Responsive Type Scale

Type sizes adapt across breakpoints. Mobile uses smaller sizes to respect viewport constraints. Desktop uses the full scale.

### Display Text (Hero Headlines)

| Token        | Mobile (default)  | Tablet (md:)      | Desktop (lg:)     |
|--------------|-------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| display-2xl  | `text-5xl`(48px)  | `text-6xl`(60px)  | `text-7xl`(72px)   |
| display-xl   | `text-4xl`(36px)  | `text-5xl`(48px)  | `text-6xl`(60px)   |
| display-lg   | `text-3xl`(30px)  | `text-4xl`(36px)  | `text-5xl`(48px)   |

### Heading Text

| Token        | Mobile (default)  | Tablet (sm:)       | Desktop (lg:)     |
|--------------|-------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| heading-xl   | `text-2xl`(24px)  | `text-3xl`(30px)  | `text-4xl`(36px)   |
| heading-lg   | `text-xl`(20px)   | `text-2xl`(24px)  | `text-3xl`(30px)   |
| heading-md   | `text-lg`(18px)   | `text-xl`(20px)   | `text-xl`(20px)    |
| heading-sm   | `text-base`(16px) | `text-base`(16px) | `text-base`(16px)  |

### Body Text

| Token        | Mobile (default)  | Tablet (sm:)       | Desktop (lg:)     |
|--------------|-------------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| body-lg      | `text-base`(16px) | `text-lg`(18px)   | `text-lg`(18px)    |
| body-md      | `text-base`(16px) | `text-base`(16px) | `text-base`(16px)  |
| body-sm      | `text-sm`(14px)   | `text-sm`(14px)   | `text-sm`(14px)    |

### Implementation Example

```html
<!-- display-2xl responsive -->
<h1 class="text-5xl font-extrabold tracking-tight sm:text-6xl lg:text-7xl">
  Hero Headline
</h1>

<!-- heading-xl responsive -->
<h2 class="text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-3xl lg:text-4xl">
  Section Title
</h2>

<!-- body-lg responsive -->
<p class="text-base leading-relaxed text-foreground sm:text-lg">
  Lead paragraph with larger text.
</p>
```

---

## 5. Heading Hierarchy Rules

### Rule 1: One H1 Per Page

Every page MUST have exactly one `<h1>`. It is the page title or hero headline.

| Page Type       | H1 Content                    | Token         |
|-----------------|-------------------------------|---------------|
| Landing Page    | Hero headline                 | display-2xl   |
| Product/Offer   | Product name + value prop     | display-xl    |
| Dashboard       | "Dashboard" or view name      | heading-xl    |
| Auth Flow       | "Sign In" / "Create Account"  | heading-lg    |
| Blog/Article    | Article title                 | display-lg    |
| Settings        | "Settings"                    | heading-xl    |

### Rule 2: Sequential Hierarchy

Headings MUST follow sequential order. Never skip levels.

```
CORRECT:                    INCORRECT:
H1 Page Title               H1 Page Title
  H2 Section                   H3 Section (skipped H2)
    H3 Subsection                H5 Detail (skipped H3, H4)
    H3 Subsection              H2 Section
  H2 Section
    H3 Subsection
      H4 Detail
```

### Rule 3: Heading Level to Semantic Token Mapping

| HTML Element | Semantic Token | Typical Tailwind                                  |
|--------------|----------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| `<h1>`       | display-* or heading-xl | `text-4xl font-bold tracking-tight sm:text-5xl lg:text-6xl` |
| `<h2>`       | heading-xl     | `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-3xl lg:text-4xl` |
| `<h3>`       | heading-lg     | `text-xl font-semibold tracking-tight sm:text-2xl lg:text-3xl` |
| `<h4>`       | heading-md     | `text-lg font-semibold sm:text-xl`                |
| `<h5>`       | heading-sm     | `text-base font-semibold`                         |
| `<h6>`       | heading-xs     | `text-sm font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide`   |

### Rule 4: Line Length

Body text MUST be constrained to **65-75 characters per line** for optimal readability.

| Method             | Tailwind Class | Max Width     | Approx Chars |
|--------------------|----------------|---------------|--------------|
| Prose width        | `max-w-prose`  | 65ch          | ~65 chars    |
| Fixed width        | `max-w-2xl`    | 672px         | ~70 chars    |
| Fixed width (wide) | `max-w-3xl`    | 768px         | ~80 chars    |

**Preferred:** `max-w-prose` for body text containers (set by character count, not pixels).

### Rule 5: Tracking (Letter Spacing)

| Size Range        | Tracking                   | Tailwind Class       |
|-------------------|----------------------------|----------------------|
| Display (5xl+)    | Tight (-0.025em)           | `tracking-tight`     |
| Heading (xl-4xl)  | Tight (-0.025em)           | `tracking-tight`     |
| Body (base-lg)    | Normal (0)                 | `tracking-normal`    |
| Caption/Overline  | Wide (0.05-0.1em)          | `tracking-wide` or `tracking-widest` |

### Rule 6: Color Hierarchy

| Text Level         | Tailwind Color Class          | Purpose               |
|--------------------|-------------------------------|-----------------------|
| Primary text       | `text-foreground`             | Headings, body text   |
| Secondary text     | `text-muted-foreground`       | Descriptions, metadata|
| Accent text        | `text-primary`                | Links, emphasis       |
| Destructive text   | `text-destructive`            | Errors, warnings      |
| Inverted text      | `text-primary-foreground`     | Text on primary bg    |

---

## 6. Page Type Typography Quick Reference

| Page Type       | H1 Token      | Body Token | Tracking   | Max Width        |
|-----------------|---------------|------------|------------|------------------|
| Landing Page    | display-2xl   | body-lg    | tight      | `max-w-4xl`      |
| Product/Offer   | display-xl    | body-md    | tight      | `max-w-4xl`      |
| Dashboard       | heading-xl    | body-sm    | tight      | `max-w-screen-xl`|
| Auth Flow       | heading-lg    | body-md    | tight      | `max-w-sm`       |
| Blog/Article    | display-lg    | body-md    | tight      | `max-w-prose`    |
| Settings        | heading-xl    | body-md    | tight      | `max-w-screen-xl`|

---

## 7. Tailwind Typography Plugin (Prose)

For long-form content (blog, documentation), use the `@tailwindcss/typography` plugin:

```html
<!-- Standard prose -->
<article class="prose dark:prose-invert">
  <!-- All child elements get proper typography -->
</article>

<!-- Large prose (body-lg) -->
<article class="prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert">
  <!-- Larger base size -->
</article>

<!-- Constrained width prose -->
<article class="prose prose-lg dark:prose-invert mx-auto max-w-prose">
  <!-- Centered, readable width -->
</article>
```

### Prose Customization

| Modifier            | Tailwind Class               | Effect                       |
|---------------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Size: small         | `prose-sm`                   | 14px base                    |
| Size: default       | `prose`                      | 16px base                    |
| Size: large         | `prose-lg`                   | 18px base                    |
| Size: extra-large   | `prose-xl`                   | 20px base                    |
| Dark mode           | `dark:prose-invert`          | Inverts colors for dark mode |
| Custom link color   | `prose-a:text-primary`       | Set link color               |
| Custom heading color| `prose-headings:text-foreground` | Set heading color       |

---

## 8. Cross-References

- **Spacing and vertical rhythm details:** See [spacing-rhythm-system.md](spacing-rhythm-system.md) (KB4)
- **Typography within layout patterns:** See [page-layout-framework.md](page-layout-framework.md) (KB1)
- **Copy-driven typography decisions:** See [copy-to-layout-bridge.md](copy-to-layout-bridge.md) (KB5)

---

## 9. References

- Material Design 3 Type Scale (Google)
- Modular Scale Calculator (type-scale.com) -- 1.250 Major Third
- Tailwind CSS v4 Typography documentation
- @tailwindcss/typography plugin
- Butterick's Practical Typography (line length, vertical rhythm)
- Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 (text sizing, contrast)


## Referência: references/squad/data/url-extract-prompt.pre-phase2.txt.bak

````text
You are a design system extraction expert.

You have been given evidence from a public website. Read the inputs in this order of priority:

1. **CSS variables (GROUND TRUTH — primary source):** {{CSS_VARS_PATH}}
   This file lists every `--name: value;` declaration with its selector scope. These are CANONICAL tokens declared by the source system. ALWAYS prefer these values over any inference.

2. **@font-face declarations:** {{FONT_FACES_PATH}}
   Structured list of self-hosted font faces with family + URLs + weight + style + display. This is the exhaustive type system — including italic, bold-italic, variable, and icon fonts.

3. **Token usage graph:** {{USAGE_GRAPH_PATH}}
   For each `--var`, how many times it's referenced. High `references` = canonical/used token. Low `references` = legacy/decorative. Use this to decide which tokens deserve top-level slots in the YAML frontmatter vs. extended named tokens.

4. **Per-component properties (CRITICAL for component-accurate output):** {{COMPONENT_PROPS_PATH}}
   For each component class (button / card / input / badge / link / nav / tab), the parser walks the CSS and extracts every `border-radius`, `padding`, `font-weight`, `font-size`, `border-width`, `background-color`, `color` declaration found inside selectors that match `.btn`, `.button`, `button`, `.card`, `.input`, `input`, `.badge`, etc.
   - The `most_common` value per property is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for that component's resolved style.
   - Example: if `summary.button["border-radius"].most_common` is `"0"`, the buttons in this design system are SQUARE — even if `--radius-md: 8px` exists in the var inventory.
   - **NEVER infer button radius from `rounded.md`. ALWAYS use `summary.button["border-radius"].most_common` when present.**
   - The same rule applies to `card`, `input`, `badge`.
   - Reflect this in the `preview_tokens` block: `button_radius`, `card_radius`, `input_radius` — emit them when the component-properties data has clear most_common values.
   - **NEW (variant matrix):** `summary[component].states` lists all detected interactive states (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`). Use these properties to reflect correctly in `preview_tokens` when emitting hover/focus colors, OR document in `## Components` prose if state-specific behavior is significant.
   - **NEW (variants):** `summary[component].variants` lists variants detected via BEM (`--primary`, `--ghost`) or attr (`[data-variant]`). Reflect in `## Components` prose when ≥2 variants are found — signals to the LLM that the component is multi-variant.
   - Backward compat: `summary[component][property]` (top level) still exists and is equivalent to `summary[component].states.default[property]`.

5. **Regex token candidates:** {{TOKENS_PATH}}
   Heuristic pass: hex/rgb/hsl colors, font-sizes, weights, radii, spacing values found anywhere in the CSS.

6. **Concatenated CSS:** {{CSS_PATH}}
   Everything from `<link rel="stylesheet">`, `<link rel="preload" as="style">`, `@import` (resolved 1 level), inline `<style>` blocks, and `style=""` attrs.

7. **Page markdown:** {{HTML_MD_PATH}}
   Turndown of the HTML for context (brand name, tone, page copy).

8. **Stack fingerprint:** {{STACK_PATH}}
   Detected technology stack (frameworks, CSS frameworks, component libraries, design systems).
   Use this signal to bias **conventions**, not tokens:
   - Webflow / Wix / Squarespace → builder-proprietary class names, expect auto-generated `.w-` / `wix-` markup.
   - Next.js + shadcn/ui → Radix primitives + Tailwind utilities preferred.
   - WordPress → semantic HTML but token system is theme-dependent — verify CSS vars before assuming.
   - Apple / Anthropic / Vercel design systems → respect the proprietary token namespace (`--sk-`, `--anthropic-`, `--geist-`); do not coerce to Tailwind defaults.
   Do NOT generate framework-specific code — only align naming conventions and component anatomy with the detected origin.

9. **Style archetype (visual classification):** {{STYLE_FINGERPRINT_PATH}}
   Detected primary archetype: **{{ARCHETYPE}}**
   This complements the technical stack signal — it tells you HOW the design feels, not what tools it uses.
   Possible values: shadcn-neutral, carbon-enterprise, material-elevation, polaris-friendly, apple-glass, brutalist-mono, govuk-conservative, porsche-precision, ant-china-enterprise, marketing-gradient, community-polished, unclassified.
   Use the archetype to bias **prose voice** in the DESIGN.md narrative sections (Overview, Colors rationale, Typography rationale):
   - shadcn-neutral / brutalist-mono → terse, dev-tooling tone, function-over-form
   - carbon-enterprise / govuk-conservative → information-density, accessibility-first, civic vocabulary
   - apple-glass / marketing-gradient → premium consumer voice, generous whitespace narrative
   - polaris-friendly / community-polished → optimistic e-commerce / open-source warmth
   - material-elevation → mobile-first, tonal palette vocabulary
   - porsche-precision / ant-china-enterprise → branded mono-with-accent, technical typography
   The archetype must NOT change the tokens you extract — only the words you use to describe them.

Your task: Generate a DESIGN.md file following Google's open DESIGN.md specification.
Reference: https://github.com/google-labs-code/design.md

The DESIGN.md format uses YAML frontmatter for machine-readable tokens, followed by markdown sections explaining the design rationale.

## YAML Frontmatter (between --- delimiters)

Extract these:

- `name`: brand/site name visible on the page
- `colors`:
    - `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `neutral`, `surface`, `text`, `text-muted`, `border`, `error`, `success` — required slots, mapped from CSS vars when possible
    - Include extended named tokens (clay, lime, olive, etc.) as additional keys when they appear as named CSS vars
    - **CRITICAL — `primary` is the BRAND IDENTITY color, not the most-used UI color.**
      The brand identity color is the one a person would name when describing the brand: it appears in the **logo**, the **header band**, the **brand mark / favicon**, and the **first hero element**. It is often used SPARINGLY across the rest of the page.
      The most-used UI color (links, body CTAs, table headers) is frequently a SECONDARY action color — blues are over-represented because every link defaults to blue.
      Examples of brands where the identity color is NOT the most-used UI color:
        - **Mercado Livre:** identity = yellow `#ffe600` (logo, header band) · UI-heavy = blue `#3483fa` (links, listings). primary=yellow, secondary=blue.
        - **McDonald's:** identity = yellow + red. UI links would be a generic blue. primary=yellow.
        - **IKEA:** identity = blue + yellow. UI = neutrals. primary=blue.
        - **Spotify:** identity = green `#1DB954` (logo). UI = mostly black/gray. primary=green.
        - **Stripe:** identity = purple `#635bff` (logo, hero gradient). UI = black/gray. primary=purple.
      How to decide:
        1. Look at the brand name extracted (`name`) and your prior knowledge of the brand's iconic color. If you know the brand, trust that.
        2. Look at `<header>` or top-band background colors and `og:image` / favicon hex hints.
        3. ONLY if no brand identity signal exists, fall back to the most-prominent CTA color.
      If the page archetype is `polaris-friendly`, do NOT default to blue primary by association — Polaris is one specific brand, not a license to assume blue. Apply the same identity-not-UI logic.
- `typography`:
    - `h1`, `h2`, `h3`, `h4`, `body-lg`, `body-md`, `body-sm`, `label`, `mono` — when present
    - Each entry: `{ fontFamily, fontSize, fontWeight, lineHeight, letterSpacing }`
    - Use exact font-family from `@font-face.family` or from CSS var `--font--*` declarations
- `rounded`: `{ none, sm, md, lg, full }` in px (or in the source's native keying if non-conventional)
- `spacing`: `{ xs, sm, md, lg, xl }` in px (or native keying)
- `preview_tokens` (REQUIRED — used by the live component preview):
    A flat map of resolved 6-digit hex values keyed by intent. The preview consumer
    reads this block FIRST when rendering buttons / cards / inputs, then falls back
    to CSS var lookup, then to `colors.*`. Filling this block correctly is the
    single highest-impact thing you can do for visual fidelity of the preview.

    Required keys (emit ALL — use the closest semantic match if a dedicated token
    is missing, and document the inference in the `## Components` prose section):

    ```yaml
    preview_tokens:
      button_primary_bg: "#0071e3"        # the fill color of the most prominent CTA
      button_primary_text: "#ffffff"      # the text color on top of button_primary_bg
      button_primary_border: "#0071e3"    # usually same as bg unless source has explicit border
      button_secondary_bg: "transparent"  # most secondary buttons are outlined or ghost
      button_secondary_text: "#1d1d1f"    # text color of secondary
      button_secondary_border: "#d2d2d7"  # the outline color
      button_tertiary_text: "#0066cc"     # usually the link color (no bg/border)
      surface_bg: "#ffffff"               # default page background
      card_bg: "#f5f5f7"                  # card / elevated surface
      text: "#1d1d1f"                     # default body text
      text_muted: "#6e6e73"               # secondary text
      border: "#d2d2d7"                   # default hairline
      accent: "#0071e3"                   # brand accent (often = primary, sometimes distinct)
      # Per-component dimensions — pull from {{COMPONENT_PROPS_PATH}} most_common values
      button_radius: "9999px"             # button border-radius (980px pill for Apple, 0 for AIOX cockpit, 8px for Anthropic)
      card_radius: "16px"                 # card border-radius
      input_radius: "5px"                 # input border-radius
    ```

    Resolution priority (use this order):
    1. The site's most prominent visible CTA — the actual button you can see in screenshots
       of `apple.com`, `linear.app`, etc. If the source CSS has tokens like
       `--sk-button-background` (Apple), `--btn-primary-bg` (generic), or
       `--cta-bg`, that's `button_primary_bg`. Resolve them to 6-digit hex.
    2. Generic --button-* tokens (Anthropic-style: `--button-primary--background`)
    3. Generic semantic tokens (`--primary`, `--brand`, `--action`)
    4. The most-referenced color in the usage graph that isn't `--text` or `--background`

    These values are RESOLVED — convert any `var(...)` chain or `rgb(...)` form to
    a 6-digit hex string. The preview cannot resolve `var()` — it just renders inline.

## Temporary provenance comments (B4 — REQUIRED, stripped from final DESIGN.md)

For each top-level token, append a YAML comment at end of line indicating its origin.
These comments are used only by the extraction pipeline to build `extraction-log.yaml`;
the final compiled `DESIGN.md` strips them to stay compact for downstream LLM usage.

```yaml
colors:
  primary: "#d97757"      # from --swatch--clay
  secondary: "#141413"    # from --swatch--slate-dark
  tertiary: "#c6613f"     # inferred from primary darker variant
typography:
  h1:
    fontFamily: "Anthropic Serif, Georgia, serif"   # from --font--serif (CSS var)
    fontSize: 4.5rem                                  # from h1 font-size declaration
```

Origin categories:
- `from --var-name` — sourced from a CSS variable in {{CSS_VARS_PATH}}
- `from @font-face` — sourced from a @font-face declaration in {{FONT_FACES_PATH}}
- `from <selector> declaration` — sourced from a non-var CSS rule
- `inferred from <reasoning>` — when no direct CSS source exists; explain briefly

## Markdown Body (after frontmatter)

Write these sections:
- `## Overview` — 1-2 sentence design philosophy
- `## Colors` — explain each color's semantic role
- `## Typography` — describe the hierarchy and when to use each
- `## Layout` — spacing system, radius philosophy, grid patterns
- `## Components` — describe key UI components implied by the CSS (buttons, cards, inputs, navigation)

## Rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE)

- Use EXACT hex codes from {{CSS_VARS_PATH}} when available. The CSS variables file is THE GROUND TRUTH.
- Font families must match `@font-face.family` exactly when self-hosted faces exist.
- Do NOT invent font names. Do NOT estimate hex values when a CSS var declares them.
- Every top-level token in the frontmatter MUST carry a provenance comment.
- You do NOT have a screenshot. The CSS files are the visual evidence.
- Output ONLY the DESIGN.md content. No preamble, no explanation, no markdown code fences around the whole document.

## Spec-clean output (REQUIRED to pass `@google/design.md lint`)

The `@google/design.md` linter enforces strict types on the YAML frontmatter. Apply these conversions BEFORE writing the file:

### Colors — only 6-digit hex (NO alpha)

- ✅ `"#d97757"` — 6-digit hex
- ❌ `"#1414131a"` — 8-digit hex (with alpha) is REJECTED
- ❌ `"rgba(...)"` — RGBA functions are also REJECTED by the lint
- ❌ `"hsl(...)"` — HSL functions are also REJECTED

If the source CSS uses 8-digit hex (alpha) or rgba/hsl, **drop the alpha component and emit only the 6-digit base hex**:
- `#1414131a` → `"#141413"`
- `#14141333` → `"#141413"`
- `#faf9f51a` → `"#faf9f5"`
- `rgba(20, 20, 19, 0.1)` → `"#141413"`

Document the alpha loss in the provenance comment: `# from --swatch--slate-faded-10 (alpha 0.1 dropped — spec accepts only 6-digit hex)`.

For tokens that conceptually NEED alpha (borders, overlays), emit the alpha discussion in the `## Colors` prose section, not in the frontmatter.

### Dimensions (rounded, spacing, letterSpacing) — must carry a unit

- ✅ `0px`, `4px`, `1rem`, `0.5em`, `-0.02em`
- ❌ `0` — bare number is REJECTED. Always emit `0px`.
- ❌ `normal` — keyword REJECTED for `letterSpacing`. Convert to `0em`.
- ❌ `100vw`, `50vh`, `5%` — viewport / percentage units REJECTED. Convert:
  - `100vw` (pill / full-round) → emit `9999px` (functionally equivalent for radius)
  - viewport-based spacing → omit from frontmatter, document in `## Layout` prose instead

### Required slots

`colors:` MUST include all required semantic slots even if the source has no dedicated token:
- `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `neutral`, `surface`, `text`, `text-muted`, `border`, `error`, `success`

When the source lacks a dedicated token (e.g., `error`, `success`):
- Pick the closest semantic match from the available palette
- Mark the provenance as `# inferred from <reasoning>`
- Do NOT omit the slot — emit it with an inferred value

### Components block

The `@google/design.md` linter v0.1.0 has a known bug parsing deeply nested `components:` blocks. To avoid the bug:
- DESCRIBE components in the `## Components` markdown section (prose) — this is the recommended path
- DO NOT emit a `components:` YAML block in the frontmatter with nested variant/state objects
- If you must reference component tokens, list them as flat top-level keys at the document level (not nested inside `components:`)

### Default theme — extract the visible theme, not the first :root rule

**Detected default theme: `{{DEFAULT_THEME}}` (confidence: {{THEME_CONFIDENCE}})**

This site renders in `{{DEFAULT_THEME}}` mode by default. When the CSS has BOTH light and dark variants for the same token (e.g. `--bg` defined both in `:root` and `[data-theme="dark"]`):

- ✅ **DO** prefer values from the `{{DEFAULT_THEME}}` scope. If `{{DEFAULT_THEME}}` is `dark`, look for selectors like `[data-theme="dark"]`, `.dark`, `.dark-theme`, `[data-color-mode="dark"]` and use those values for `surface`, `text`, `background`, `border`.
- ✅ **DO** verify visually: if the site renders dark, `surface` should be a dark hex (luminance < 0.3), `text` should be light. Inverted = wrong theme picked.
- ❌ **DON'T** default to `:root` values when the site is `dark` — `:root` often holds light defaults that get overridden by JS-applied `data-theme="dark"` at runtime.
- ❌ **DON'T** invent both — emit ONE canonical value per slot reflecting the default theme. (If you want to document the alternate theme, do it in `## Colors` prose.)

When `{{DEFAULT_THEME}}` is `light`, the standard `:root` extraction is usually correct. When it's `dark`, you must consciously select the dark variant.

### Coverage Notes — communicate intentional absences

Some token categories may be ABSENT from the source CSS. When you detect that the site does NOT use a feature, **state it explicitly in the appropriate prose section** so downstream consumers don't try to invent it:

- **Flat design (no shadows, mostly `box-shadow: none`)** → in `## Elevation & Depth`, write a sentence like: *"The system is intentionally low-elevation. Depth is communicated via border + surface contrast, not shadow."* Add to `## Don'ts`: *"Don't add layered shadows."*
- **No glassmorphism (no `backdrop-filter`)** → in `## Don'ts`: *"Don't add backdrop-blur. The visual language relies on solid surfaces."*
- **No tooltips/avatars/tabs** → in `## Components`: *"This surface does not define tooltip / avatar / tab tokens. If your context requires them, follow the typography + radius + spacing primitives to derive consistent ones."*
- **Single button style (no variants)** → in `## Components > Button`: *"The system uses a single button style. There is no secondary/ghost/outline variant — emphasis is conveyed by placement and copy."*
- **Marketing-only surface (no forms)** → in `## Components`: *"This is a marketing surface — labels, help-text, and form-error tokens are not defined here. If you ship a form on this brand, infer label sizing from `body-sm` and helper from `caption`."*

Write these as DESIGN INTENT, not as extraction failures. The reader should understand "the brand chose not to use X" rather than "the extractor missed X".

Source URL: {{URL}}

Write the DESIGN.md to: {{OUTPUT_PATH}}

Use the Write tool to create the file. Do not output the content to stdout.
````

````text
You are a design system extraction expert.

Before reading site evidence, load and obey this process contract:

0. **Process contract (NON-NEGOTIABLE — loaded data):** {{PROCESS_CONTRACT_PATH}}

{{PROCESS_CONTRACT}}

You have been given evidence from a public website. Read the inputs in this order of priority:

1. **CSS variables (GROUND TRUTH — primary source):** {{CSS_VARS_PATH}}
   This file lists every `--name: value;` declaration with its selector scope. These are CANONICAL tokens declared by the source system. ALWAYS prefer these values over any inference.

2. **@font-face declarations:** {{FONT_FACES_PATH}}
   Structured list of self-hosted font faces with family + URLs + weight + style + display. This is the exhaustive type system — including italic, bold-italic, variable, and icon fonts.

3. **Token usage graph:** {{USAGE_GRAPH_PATH}}
   For each `--var`, how many times it's referenced. High `references` = canonical/used token. Low `references` = legacy/decorative. Use this to decide which tokens deserve top-level slots in the YAML frontmatter vs. extended named tokens.

   **CRITICAL — `references` count is a USAGE-FREQUENCY signal, NOT a brand-identity signal.**
   A color used 200× across links and table headers is a UI accent, not necessarily the brand color. NEVER select `colors.primary` from the highest-references token. See the brand-identity rule under `colors` below.

4. **Per-component properties (CRITICAL for component-accurate output):** {{COMPONENT_PROPS_PATH}}
   For each component class (button / card / input / badge / link / nav / tab), the parser walks the CSS and extracts every `border-radius`, `padding`, `font-weight`, `font-size`, `border-width`, `background-color`, `color` declaration found inside selectors that match `.btn`, `.button`, `button`, `.card`, `.input`, `input`, `.badge`, etc.
   - The `most_common` value per property is the SOURCE OF TRUTH for that component's resolved style.
   - Example: if `summary.button["border-radius"].most_common` is `"0"`, the buttons in this design system are SQUARE — even if `--radius-md: 8px` exists in the var inventory.
   - **NEVER infer button radius from `rounded.md`. ALWAYS use `summary.button["border-radius"].most_common` when present.**
   - The same rule applies to `card`, `input`, `badge`.
   - Reflect this in the `preview_tokens` block: `button_radius`, `card_radius`, `input_radius` — emit them when the component-properties data has clear most_common values.
   - **Variant matrix:** `summary[component].states` lists all detected interactive states (`default`, `hover`, `focus`, `focus-visible`, `active`, `disabled`). Use these properties to reflect correctly in `preview_tokens` when emitting hover/focus colors, AND emit them as named atoms in the `components:` YAML block (see Components section below).
   - **Variants:** `summary[component].variants` lists variants detected via BEM (`--primary`, `--ghost`) or attr (`[data-variant]`). When ≥2 variants are found, emit each as a named atom (e.g. `button-primary`, `button-ghost`).
   - Backward compat: `summary[component][property]` (top level) still exists and is equivalent to `summary[component].states.default[property]`.

5. **Interaction state evidence:** {{COMPONENT_STATES_PATH}}
   Source selector evidence for `:hover`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `:active`, `:disabled`, attribute states, and compound states such as `:disabled:hover`.
   Use this file to distinguish an intentional flat state model from missing data. If `states_absent` includes focus, do not invent focus styling; document the absence as an accessibility/design-system gap unless `focus-ring.json` has extracted evidence.
   Use `state_value_palette` for hover/focus/disabled preview tokens and component prose when it agrees with component CSS declarations.

6. **Motion primitives:** {{MOTION_PATH}}
   This file includes `durations`, `easings`, `transitions[]`, `keyframes[]`, and `keyframe_bodies{}`. Use `transitions[]` to describe which properties move, how quickly, and with which timing curve.
   If `keyframe_bodies{}` contains a real source keyframe, quote only the keyframe name and summarize the motion; do not paste large CSS bodies into DESIGN.md.

7. **Brand asymmetry signals:** {{ASYMMETRIES_PATH}}
   This file lists extracted signals such as radii flatness, shadow absence, transition uniformity, narrow palettes, missing focus states, and disabled opacity patterns.
   Treat asymmetries as brand identity evidence, not defects by default. Example: "flat, shadowless interface" is valid when the CSS proves it.

8. **Selector provenance:** {{SELECTOR_PROVENANCE_PATH}}
   Per-token source selector graph. Use this to resolve conflicts between generic variables and component-specific declarations.
   Prefer values with direct selector/property evidence over generic token names when writing provenance comments, component recipes, and preview tokens.

9. **Atomic selector classification:** {{ATOMIC_CLASSIFICATION_PATH}}

10. **Regex token candidates:** {{TOKENS_PATH}}

11. **Concatenated CSS:** {{CSS_PATH}}

12. **Page markdown:** {{HTML_MD_PATH}}

13. **Stack fingerprint:** {{STACK_PATH}}

   The archetype must NOT change the tokens you extract — only the words you use to describe them.
````
